translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 66
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Governance, Volume 66

sentences.zh: 【漢紀五十八】起屠維赤奮若，盡昭陽大荒落，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Han Records 58] Beginning with Tuyu Chifenruo, ending with Zhaoyang Dahuangluo, five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Han Records 58] Spanning from the year Tuyu Chifenruo through Zhaoyang Dahuangluo—a period of five years.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝辛

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [xin]
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han

sentences.zh: 春，三月，曹操軍至譙。

translations.literal: Spring, third month, Cao Cao's army reached Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the third month, Cao Cao's army arrived at Qiao.

sentences.zh: 孫權圍合肥，久不下。

translations.literal: Sun Quan besieged Hefei; for a long time he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan laid siege to Hefei but could not capture it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 權率輕騎欲身往突敵，長史張紘諫曰：「夫兵者凶器，戰者危事也。

translations.literal: Quan led light cavalry and wished to charge the enemy in person; Chief Clerk Zhang Hong remonstrated, saying: "Weapons are instruments of ill omen, and battle is a perilous affair.
translations.idiomatic: Quan led light cavalry and intended to charge the enemy himself. Chief Clerk Zhang Hong remonstrated: "Weapons are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is a perilous business.

sentences.zh: 今麾下恃盛壯之氣，忽強暴之虜，三軍之眾，莫不寒心。

translations.literal: Now your forces rely on their vigorous strength and confront a fierce foe; the whole army is without exception filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Your troops now lean on their peak morale to face a brutal enemy, and the entire army is gripped with fear.

sentences.zh: 雖斬將搴旗，威震敵場，此乃偏將之任，非主將之宜也。

translations.literal: Though one slays generals and seizes banners, shaking the enemy field with awe—this is the task of a lieutenant, not what a commander-in-chief should do.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you slay enemy generals and seize their banners, winning glory on the battlefield—that is work for a subordinate commander, not for the supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 願抑賁、育之勇，懷霸王之計。

translations.literal: I pray you restrain the courage of Ben and Yu and embrace the strategy of a hegemon-king.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to curb the raw daring of warriors like Ben and Yu and instead embrace the grand strategy of a hegemon.

sentences.zh: 」權乃止。

translations.literal: " Quan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " With that, Quan desisted.

sentences.zh: 曹操遣將軍張喜將兵解圍，久而未至。

translations.literal: Cao Cao sent General Zhang Xi with troops to relieve the siege, but for a long time he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dispatched General Zhang Xi with troops to lift the siege, but they were long in coming.

sentences.zh: 揚州別駕楚國蔣濟密白刺史，偽得喜書，云步騎四萬已到雩婁，遣主簿迎喜。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Vice-Director Jiang Ji of Chu secretly informed the Inspector, forging a letter from Xi saying forty thousand infantry and cavalry had reached Yulu, and sent the chief clerk to meet Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji of Chu, vice-director of Yangzhou, secretly informed the inspector. He forged a letter from Zhang Xi claiming that forty thousand foot and horse troops had already reached Yulu, and sent the chief clerk to welcome Xi.

sentences.zh: 三部使繼書語城中守將，一部得入城，二部為權兵所得。

translations.literal: Three messengers in succession carried letters speaking to the defenders in the city; one group entered the city, two groups were taken by Quan's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Three messengers in succession delivered letters to the city's defenders. One party got inside; the other two were captured by Quan's forces.

sentences.zh: 權信之，遽燒圍走。

translations.literal: Quan believed it and hastily burned the encampment and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quan believed the report, burned his siege works, and withdrew in haste.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，曹操引水軍自渦入淮，出肥水，軍合肥，開芍陂屯田。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Cao Cao led his navy from the Wo into the Huai, out onto the Fei, encamped at Hefei, and opened the Quepi for garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, Cao Cao led his fleet from the Wo River into the Huai, then out onto the Fei River. He stationed his army at Hefei and opened the Quepi reservoir for military colony farming.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，荊州地震。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Jing province had an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, an earthquake struck Jing province.

sentences.zh: 十二月，操軍還譙。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Cao's army returned to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Cao Cao's army returned to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 廬江人陳蘭、梅成據灊、六叛，操遣蕩寇將軍張遼討斬之；

translations.literal: Chen Lan and Mei Cheng of Lujiang held Qian and Liu in rebellion; Cao sent the Pacifying Bandits General Zhang Liao to attack and execute them;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lan and Mei Cheng of Lujiang seized Qian and Liu in rebellion. Cao Cao sent the Pacifying Bandits General Zhang Liao to campaign against them and put them to death;

sentences.zh: 因使遼與樂進、李典等將七千餘人屯合肥。

translations.literal: thereupon he had Liao camp at Hefei with Yue Jin, Li Dian, and others commanding more than seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: he then stationed Liao at Hefei together with Yue Jin, Li Dian, and others, with a garrison of more than seven thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 周瑜攻曹仁歲餘，所殺傷甚眾，仁委城走。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu attacked Cao Ren for more than a year; those killed and wounded were very numerous, and Ren abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu besieged Cao Ren for more than a year. Casualties on both sides were heavy, and in the end Ren abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 權以瑜領南郡太守，屯據江陵；

translations.literal: Quan had Yu serve as Grand Administrator of Nan commandery, stationed at Jiangling;
translations.idiomatic: Quan appointed Zhou Yu Grand Administrator of Nan commandery, with his base at Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 程普領江夏太守，治沙羨；

translations.literal: Cheng Pu served as Grand Administrator of Jiangxia, administering from Shaxian;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu was made Grand Administrator of Jiangxia, with his seat at Shaxian;

sentences.zh: 呂范領彭澤太守；

translations.literal: Lü Fan served as Grand Administrator of Pengze;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan was made Grand Administrator of Pengze;

sentences.zh: 呂蒙領尋陽令。

translations.literal: Lü Meng served as magistrate of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: and Lü Meng was appointed magistrate of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 劉備表權行車騎將軍，領徐州牧。

translations.literal: Liu Bei memorialized that Quan should act as General of Chariots and Cavalry and hold the governorship of Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei submitted a memorial recommending that Sun Quan be appointed acting General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 會劉琦卒，權以備領荊州牧，周瑜分南岸地以給備。

translations.literal: When Liu Qi died, Quan had Bei serve as Governor of Jing province; Zhou Yu divided southern-bank territory to give to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qi died, Quan appointed Liu Bei Governor of Jing province, and Zhou Yu allotted him territory on the southern bank of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 備立營於油口，改名公安。

translations.literal: Bei established a camp at Youkou and renamed it Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Bei established his camp at Youkou and renamed the place Gong'an, "Public Peace."

sentences.zh: 權以妹妻備。

translations.literal: Quan gave his younger sister in marriage to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan gave his sister to Liu Bei in marriage.

sentences.zh: 妹才捷剛猛，有諸兄風，侍婢百餘人，皆執刀侍立，備每入，心常凜凜。

translations.literal: The sister was talented, sharp, and fierce, with the spirit of her elder brothers; more than a hundred maid-servants, all bearing swords, stood in attendance; whenever Bei entered, his heart would always tremble with dread.
translations.idiomatic: The sister was clever, forceful, and fierce, with something of her brothers' spirit. More than a hundred maidservants, all armed with swords, stood guard around her. Whenever Bei went in to see her, his heart would fill with dread.

sentences.zh: 曹操密遣九江蔣幹往說周瑜。

translations.literal: Cao Cao secretly sent Jiang Gan of Jiujiang to persuade Zhou Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao secretly dispatched Jiang Gan of Jiujiang to win Zhou Yu over.

sentences.zh: 幹以才辨獨步於江、淮之間，乃布衣葛巾，自托私行詣瑜。

translations.literal: Gan's eloquence was unmatched between the Yangtze and Huai; he came in plain robes and hemp headcloth, presenting himself as traveling on private business to visit Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan's eloquence was unrivaled between the Yangtze and the Huai. He came in plain cloth and a hemp headcloth, presenting himself as a private traveler when he called on Zhou Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑜出迎之，立謂幹曰：「子翼良苦，遠涉江湖，為曹氏作說客邪？

translations.literal: Yu went out to welcome him and at once said to Gan: "Ziyi, you have toiled hard, crossing rivers and lakes to be a lobbyist for the Cao clan, have you not?
translations.idiomatic: Yu went out to welcome him and said at once: "Ziyi, you have traveled far across rivers and lakes—have you come as a lobbyist for the House of Cao?

sentences.zh: 」因延幹，與周觀營中，行視倉庫、軍資、器仗訖，還飲宴，示之侍者服飾珍玩之物。

translations.literal: " He then kept Gan and toured the camp with him, inspecting storehouses, military supplies, and weapons; when they returned he feasted him and showed him the attendants' finery and curios.
translations.idiomatic: " He then detained Gan and led him on a tour of the camp, inspecting the storehouses, military supplies, and weapons. When they returned, he held a feast and displayed for him the fine garments and curios of his attendants.

sentences.zh: 因謂幹曰：「丈夫處世，遇知己之主，外托君臣之義，內結骨肉之恩，言行計從，禍福共之，假使蘇、張共生，能移其意乎？

translations.literal: He told Gan: "When a man takes his place in the world and meets a lord who truly knows him, outwardly he relies on the bond of lord and minister, inwardly he shares the affection of flesh and bone; word and deed follow that lord's will, fortune and misfortune are shared—if Su Qin and Zhang Yi were reborn together, could they shift my intent?
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Gan: "When a man meets a lord who truly understands him, outwardly he serves as minister, inwardly he is bound as kin. Word and deed follow that lord, and fortune and misfortune are shared. Even if Su Qin and Zhang Yi were alive together, could they turn my heart?

sentences.zh: 」幹但笑，終無所言。

translations.literal: " Gan only laughed and in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Gan only laughed and in the end said nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 還白操，稱瑜雅量高致，非言辭所能間也。

translations.literal: Returning, he reported to Cao, praising Yu's lofty mind and lofty bearing—no eloquence could drive him apart.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned and reported to Cao Cao, he praised Zhou Yu's magnanimity and lofty character, saying that no eloquence could drive a wedge between him and his lord.

sentences.zh: 丞相掾和洽言於曹操曰：「天下之人，材德各殊，不可一節取也。

translations.literal: He Qia, an aide in the Chancellor's office, said to Cao Cao: "The people under Heaven each differ in talent and virtue; one cannot select them all by a single standard.
translations.idiomatic: He Qia, an aide in the chancellor's office, said to Cao Cao: "The people of the realm differ in talent and virtue. One cannot judge them all by a single standard.

sentences.zh: 儉素過中，自以處身則可，以此格物，所失或多。

translations.literal: Frugality carried to excess may suit one's own conduct, but applying it as the measure for others often causes many errors.
translations.idiomatic: Frugality taken to excess may be fine for one's own conduct, but using it as the measure for everyone else often leads to grave mistakes.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷之議，吏有著新衣、乘好車者，謂之不清；

translations.literal: Now court opinion holds that an official who wears new clothes or rides a fine carriage is called corrupt;
translations.idiomatic: Nowadays at court, any official who wears new clothes or rides a fine carriage is called corrupt;

sentences.zh: 形容不飾、衣裘敝壞者，謂之廉潔。

translations.literal: one whose appearance is unadorned and whose fur cloak is worn out is called incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: while anyone whose appearance is plain and whose fur cloak is threadbare is called incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 至令士大夫故污辱其衣，藏其輿服；

translations.literal: To the point that scholars and grandees deliberately soil their garments and hide their carriages and robes;
translations.idiomatic: It has reached the point that scholars and officials deliberately soil their clothes and hide their carriages and fine robes;

sentences.zh: 朝府大吏，或自挈壺飧以入官寺。

translations.literal: some high officials of court and province even carry their own food in a basket when they enter government offices.
translations.idiomatic: and some high officials of the court and provinces even carry their own meals in baskets when they enter government offices.

sentences.zh: 夫立教觀俗，貴處中庸，為可繼也。

translations.literal: In establishing instruction and setting custom, what is prized is a mean that can be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing instruction and shaping custom, what matters is a sustainable middle path.

sentences.zh: 今崇一概難堪之行以檢殊塗，勉而為之，必有疲瘁。

translations.literal: Now to exalt one uniform standard of conduct beyond endurance as the test for every different path, and force men to comply—there will surely be exhaustion and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: To exalt one unbearable standard of conduct as the test for every different path, and force people to comply, will surely exhaust and ruin them.

sentences.zh: 古之大教，務在通人情而已。

translations.literal: The great teaching of antiquity was simply to reach through to human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The great teaching of antiquity was simply to reach through to human nature.

sentences.zh: 凡激詭之行，則容隱偽矣。

translations.literal: Whatever is contrived and contrary will harbor concealment and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever conduct is forced and unnatural, hypocrisy is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 」操善之。

translations.literal: " Cao approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao approved of his advice.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝辛建安十五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [xin], fifteenth year of Jian'an (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han, fifteenth year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公元二一零年）

translations.literal: gengyin, AD 210)
translations.idiomatic: gengyin, AD 210)

sentences.zh: 春，下令曰：「孟公綽為趙、魏老則優，不可以為滕、薛大夫。

translations.literal: Spring, an edict was issued: "Meng Gongchuo would excel as elder for Zhao and Wei but is not fit to be a grand officer of Teng or Xue.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, an edict was issued: "Meng Gongchuo would excel as steward for the houses of Zhao and Wei, but he is not fit to serve as a grand officer of Teng or Xue.

sentences.zh: 若必廉士而後可用，則齊桓其何以霸世！

translations.literal: If one must use only incorrupt men before employing them, how could Duke Huan of Qi have dominated the age!
translations.idiomatic: If only the incorrupt may be employed, how could Duke Huan of Qi ever have dominated his age!

sentences.zh: 二三子其佐我明揚仄陋，唯才是舉，吾得而用之！

translations.literal: Gentlemen, assist me in elevating the obscure and the lowly—appoint by talent alone, and I shall employ you!
translations.idiomatic: Assist me in bringing forward the obscure and the humble—recommend men for their talent alone, and I will employ them!

sentences.zh: 二月，乙巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Second month, on the first day of the month (yisi), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day (yisi), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 冬，曹操作銅爵台於鄴。

translations.literal: Winter, Cao Cao built the Bronze Bird Terrace at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Cao Cao built the Bronze Bird Terrace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己亥，操下令曰：「孤始舉孝廉，自以本非巖穴知名之士，恐為世人之所凡愚，欲好作政教以立名譽，故在濟南，除殘去穢，平心選舉。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on day jihai, Cao issued an edict: "When I first was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, I considered myself not a noted scholar from seclusion in cliffs and caves, and feared I would be judged dull by the world; I wished to do well in governance and instruction to build a reputation, so in Ji'nan I eliminated the vicious and purged the corrupt and conducted elections with an even hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day jihai, Cao Cao issued an edict: "When I was first recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, I knew I was no famous recluse from mountain caves, and feared the world would judge me ordinary. I wished to excel in governance and instruction to build a reputation. In Ji'nan I eliminated the vicious and purged corruption, conducting elections with an even hand.

sentences.zh: 以是為強豪所忿，恐致家禍，故以病還鄉里。

translations.literal: Because of this I earned the hatred of powerful clans; fearing disaster for my family, I resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: For this the powerful clans hated me. Fearing disaster for my household, I resigned on grounds of illness and returned to my home district.

sentences.zh: 時年紀尚少，乃於譙東五十里築精舍，欲秋夏讀書，冬春射獵，為二十年規，待天下清乃出仕耳。

translations.literal: I was still young then; east of Qiao I built a retreat fifty li away, intending to read in summer and autumn and hunt in winter and spring—a twenty-year plan, waiting until the realm was pacified before entering office.
translations.idiomatic: I was still young then. Fifty li east of Qiao I built a study retreat, planning to read through summer and autumn and hunt through winter and spring—a twenty-year plan, waiting until the realm was pacified before taking office.

sentences.zh: 然不能得如意，徵為典軍校尉，意遂更欲為國家討賊立功，使題墓道言『漢故征西將軍曹侯之墓』，此其志也。

translations.literal: Yet I could not have my wish; summoned as Colonel of the Palace Guard, my intent shifted—I would strike rebels for the state and win merit, having my tomb inscription read 'Tomb of Marquis Cao, Former General Who Subdues the West'—that was my aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: But I could not have my way. Summoned as Colonel of the Palace Guard, my intent changed: I would strike rebels for the state and win merit, with my tomb inscription reading 'Tomb of Marquis Cao, Former General Who Subdues the West.' That was my ambition.

sentences.zh: 而遭值董卓之難，興舉義兵。

translations.literal: But then came the calamity of Dong Zhuo, and I raised righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the calamity of Dong Zhuo, and I raised righteous troops.

sentences.zh: 後領兗州，破降黃巾三十萬眾；

translations.literal: Later I led Yan province and broke and accepted the surrender of three hundred thousand Yellow Scarves;
translations.idiomatic: Later I took command of Yan province and broke and accepted the surrender of three hundred thousand Yellow Scarves;

sentences.zh: 又討擊袁術，使窮沮而死；

translations.literal: I also attacked Yuan Shu and drove him to destitution and death;
translations.idiomatic: I attacked Yuan Shu and drove him to destitution and death;

sentences.zh: 摧破袁紹，梟其二子；

translations.literal: shattered Yuan Shao and took the heads of his two sons;
translations.idiomatic: shattered Yuan Shao and took the heads of his two sons;

sentences.zh: 復定劉表，遂平天下。

translations.literal: restored order in Liu Biao's domain and thus pacified the empire.
translations.idiomatic: restored order in Liu Biao's domain and thus pacified the empire.

sentences.zh: 身為宰相，人臣之貴已極，意望已過矣。

translations.literal: I have become Chancellor; the honor due a subject has reached its limit—my desires have already gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: I have become chancellor; the honor due a subject has reached its limit, and my ambitions have already gone too far.

sentences.zh: 設使國家無有孤，不知當幾人稱帝，幾人稱王！

translations.literal: Suppose the state had never had me—who knows how many would have styled themselves emperor, how many would have styled themselves king!
translations.idiomatic: If the state had never had me, who knows how many would have styled themselves emperor, how many would have styled themselves king!

sentences.zh: 或者人見孤強盛，又性不信天命，恐妄相忖度，言有不遜之志，每用耿耿，故為諸君陳道此言，皆肝鬲之要也。

translations.literal: Some see my power and, because I do not trust in Heaven's Mandate, fear reckless speculation, speaking of disloyal ambition; I am always troubled by this, so I lay this out for you all—these are matters from the depths of my liver and diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: Some see my power and, because I do not trust in Heaven's Mandate, fear reckless speculation and speak of disloyal ambition. This troubles me constantly, so I lay this out for you—these are matters from the depths of my heart.

sentences.zh: 然欲孤便爾委捐所典兵眾以還執事，歸就武平侯國，實不可也。

translations.literal: Yet to have me simply cast away the troops I command and return to the central administration, going back to the State of Wuping as marquis—that truly cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to have me simply cast away the troops I command, return to the central administration, and go back to my marquisate of Wuping—that truly cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 誠恐己離兵為人所禍，既為子孫計，又己敗則國家傾危，是以不得慕虛名而處實禍也！

translations.literal: Truly I fear that once I leave my army I would be harmed by others; for my descendants' sake, and because once I fail the state would totter—I cannot cherish empty fame while sitting in real peril!
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that once I leave my army I would be harmed by others. For my descendants' sake, and because if I fail the state would totter—I cannot chase empty fame while sitting in real peril!

sentences.zh: 然兼封四縣，食戶三萬，何德堪之！

translations.literal: Yet I hold four counties combined, with thirty thousand households—what virtue can deserve that!
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hold four counties combined, with thirty thousand households—what virtue could deserve that!

sentences.zh: 江湖未靜，不可讓位；

translations.literal: The rivers and lakes are not yet still; I cannot yield my post;
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not yet pacified; I cannot yield my post;

sentences.zh: 至於邑土，可得而辭。

translations.literal: as for fiefs, those may be refused.
translations.idiomatic: but as for fiefs, those I may refuse.

sentences.zh: 今上還陽夏、柘、苦三縣，戶二萬，但食武平萬戶，且以分損謗議，少減孤之責也！

translations.literal: Now I return to the court Yangxia, Zhe, and Ku counties—twenty thousand households—and keep only the ten thousand of Wuping, thereby sharing out criticism and somewhat lessening my burden.
translations.idiomatic: Now I return to the court the three counties of Yangxia, Zhe, and Ku—twenty thousand households—and keep only the ten thousand households of Wuping, thereby sharing out criticism and somewhat lessening my burden.

sentences.zh: 劉表故吏士多歸劉備，備以周瑜所給地少，不足以容其眾，乃自詣京見孫權，求都督荊州。

translations.literal: Many of Liu Biao's former clerks and gentry went over to Liu Bei; Bei found the territory Zhou Yu had given too small to hold his following, so he went in person to the capital to see Sun Quan and asked to be made Grand Protector of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Liu Biao's former officials and gentry went over to Liu Bei. Finding the territory Zhou Yu had allotted too small for his following, Bei went in person to the capital to see Sun Quan and asked to be made Grand Protector of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 瑜上疏於權曰：「劉備以梟雄之姿，而有關羽、張飛熊虎之將，必非久屈為人用者。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized Quan: "Liu Bei has the stature of a formidable hero, with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei as tiger-and-bear generals—he cannot long remain bent to serve another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu memorialized Sun Quan: "Liu Bei has the stature of a formidable hero, with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei as tiger-and-bear generals. He cannot long remain bent to serve another.

sentences.zh: 愚謂大計宜徙備置吳，盛為築宮室，多其美女玩好，以娛其耳目；

translations.literal: I humbly believe the great plan is to move Bei to Wu, build him a splendid palace, give him many beauties and fine things to delight his eyes and ears;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe the great plan is to move Liu Bei to Wu, build him a splendid palace, and give him many beauties and fine things to delight his eyes and ears;

sentences.zh: 分此二人各置一方，使如瑜者得挾與攻戰，大事可定也。

translations.literal: assign these two men each to a separate post, and let commanders like myself lead them in attack—then the great affair can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: assign Guan Yu and Zhang Fei each to a separate post, and let commanders like myself lead them in battle—then the great affair can be settled.

sentences.zh: 今猥割土地以資業之，聚此三人俱在疆場，恐蛟龍得雲雨，終非池中物也。

translations.literal: Now we rashly cede land to enrich him and gather all three on the border—fear they are dragons that, gaining cloud and rain, will not long stay pond creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Now we rashly cede land to enrich him and gather all three on the frontier. I fear that once dragons gain cloud and rain, they will not long remain creatures of a pond.

sentences.zh: 」呂范亦勸留之。

translations.literal: " Lü Fan also urged keeping him.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Fan also urged that Liu Bei be detained.

sentences.zh: 權以曹操在北，方當廣攬英雄，不從。

translations.literal: Quan, with Cao Cao in the north and needing to gather heroes broadly, did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, with Cao Cao in the north and wishing to gather heroes broadly, did not agree.

sentences.zh: 備還公安，久乃聞之，歎曰：「天下智謀之士，所見略同。

translations.literal: Bei returned to Gong'an; only after long delay did he hear of this and sigh: "The wise of the realm see much the same.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei returned to Gong'an. Only long afterward did he hear of this and sigh: "The wise of the realm see much the same.

sentences.zh: 時孔明諫孤莫行，其意亦慮此也。

translations.literal: At that time Kongming advised me not to go—his mind too feared this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kongming advised me not to go—his mind too feared this very thing.

sentences.zh: 孤方危急，不得不往，此誠險塗，殆不免周瑜之手！

translations.literal: I was in desperate straits and had to go—truly a dangerous road; I nearly fell into Zhou Yu's hands!
translations.idiomatic: I was in desperate straits and had to go. It was truly a perilous road—I nearly fell into Zhou Yu's hands!

sentences.zh: 周瑜詣京見權曰：「今曹操新政，憂在腹心，未能與將軍連兵相事也。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu went to the capital and said to Quan: "Now Cao Cao has just established his regime; his worries are at the core—he cannot yet join arms with you, General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu went to the capital and said to Sun Quan: "Cao Cao has just established his new regime. His worries are at the core—he cannot yet join arms with you, General.

sentences.zh: 乞與奮威俱進，取蜀而並張魯，因留奮威固守其地，與馬超結援，瑜還與將軍據襄陽以蹙操，北方可圖也。

translations.literal: I beg to advance with Fenyangwei, take Shu and absorb Zhang Lu, leave Fenyangwei to hold that territory and ally with Ma Chao; Yu will return with the General to hold Xiangyang and press Cao—then the north can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to advance with Fenyangwei, take Shu and absorb Zhang Lu, leave Fenyangwei to hold that territory and ally with Ma Chao. I will return with you, General, to hold Xiangyang and press Cao Cao—then the north can be taken.

sentences.zh: 」權許之。

translations.literal: " Quan assented.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan assented.

sentences.zh: 奮威者，孫堅弟子奮威將軍、丹楊太守瑜也。

translations.literal: Fenyangwei refers to Yu [Sun Yu], Sun Jian's nephew, General Who Displays Might and Grand Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fenyangwei refers to Sun Yu, Sun Jian's nephew, General Who Displays Might and Grand Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 周瑜還江陵為行裝，於道病困，與權箋曰：「修短命矣，誠不足惜；

translations.literal: Zhou Yu returned to Jiangling to prepare baggage; on the road he fell gravely ill and wrote Quan: "Xiu [Zhou Yu's style] is short-lived indeed—truly not worth grieving;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu returned to Jiangling to prepare for the campaign. On the road he fell gravely ill and wrote to Sun Quan: "Xiu is short-lived indeed—truly not worth grieving;

sentences.zh: 但恨微志未展，不復奉教命耳。

translations.literal: but I regret my small ambitions were not fulfilled and I cannot again receive your orders.
translations.idiomatic: but I regret that my small ambitions were not fulfilled and I cannot again receive your commands.

sentences.zh: 方今曹操在北，疆場未靜；

translations.literal: Now Cao Cao is in the north and the frontier is not quiet;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao is in the north and the frontier is not yet quiet;

sentences.zh: 劉備寄寓，有似養虎。

translations.literal: Liu Bei is lodged here like feeding a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei is lodged here like feeding a tiger.

sentences.zh: 天下之事，未知終始，此朝士旰食之秋，至尊垂慮之日也。

translations.literal: Affairs of the realm—who knows how they will end; this is the season when courtiers skip their meals at dawn, when Your Majesty bends in care day after day.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of the realm have no known end. This is the season when courtiers skip their meals at dawn, when Your Majesty bends in care day after day.

sentences.zh: 魯肅忠烈，臨事不苟，可以代瑜。

translations.literal: Lu Su is loyal and stern, never lax in affairs—he can replace Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su is loyal and stern, never lax in affairs—he can replace me.

sentences.zh: 儻所言可采，瑜死不朽矣！

translations.literal: If what I say may be adopted, Yu's death will not be in vain!
translations.idiomatic: If what I say may be adopted, my death will not be in vain!

sentences.zh: 」卒於巴丘。

translations.literal: " He died at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: " He died at Baling.

sentences.zh: 權聞之哀慟，曰：「公瑾有王佐之資，今忽短命，孤何賴哉！

translations.literal: When Quan heard he grieved greatly and said: "Gongjin had the talent to aid a king—now suddenly short-lived—on whom can I rely!
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan heard, he grieved deeply and said: "Gongjin had the talent to aid a king—now suddenly cut short—on whom can I rely!

sentences.zh: 」自迎其喪於蕪湖。

translations.literal: " He went in person to meet the funeral cortege at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: " He went in person to meet the funeral cortege at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 瑜有一女、二男，權為長子登娶其女；

translations.literal: Yu had one daughter and two sons; Quan had his eldest son Deng marry the daughter;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu had one daughter and two sons. Sun Quan had his eldest son Deng marry the daughter;

sentences.zh: 以其男循為騎都尉，妻以女；

translations.literal: He made his son Xun Colonel of Cavalry and gave him a daughter in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his son Xun Colonel of Cavalry and gave him a daughter in marriage;

sentences.zh: 胤為興業都尉，妻以宗女。

translations.literal: Yin was made Grand Commandant of Xingye, and a clanswoman was given him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was made Grand Commandant of Xingye, and a clanswoman of Sun Quan's house was given him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 初，瑜見友於孫策，太夫人又使權以兄奉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu had been friends with Sun Ce, and the Grand Lady Mother had also had Quan treat him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhou Yu had been close friends with Sun Ce, and the Grand Lady Mother had also instructed Sun Quan to treat him as he would an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 是時權位為將軍，諸將、賓客為禮尚簡，而瑜獨先盡敬，便執臣節。

translations.literal: At that time Quan held the rank of general; the generals and guests kept their ritual rather simple, but Yu alone was first in full respect and at once performed the rites of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sun Quan held the rank of general. The other generals and guests kept their courtesies rather informal, but Zhou Yu alone was foremost in full respect and at once performed the rites due a subject.

sentences.zh: 程普頗以年長，數陵侮瑜，瑜折節下之，終不與校。

translations.literal: Cheng Pu, relying on his greater years, several times insulted and bullied Yu; Yu bent his will and humbled himself beneath Pu, and in the end never contended with him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu, relying on his greater age, several times insulted and bullied Zhou Yu. Yu bent his will and humbled himself before Pu, and in the end never contended with him.

sentences.zh: 普後自敬服而親重之，乃告人曰：「與周公瑾交，若飲醇醪，不覺自醉。

translations.literal: Later Pu came of himself to respect and esteem him, and told others: "To associate with Gongjin Zhou is like drinking fine wine—you do not notice until you are drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cheng Pu came of his own accord to respect and esteem him, and told others: "To associate with Gongjin Zhou is like drinking fine wine—you do not notice until you are drunk.

sentences.zh: 權以魯肅為奮武校尉，代瑜領兵，令程普領南郡太守。

translations.literal: Quan made Lu Su Colonel Who Displays Martial Might, to replace Yu in command of troops, and had Cheng Pu serve as Grand Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan made Lu Su Colonel Who Displays Martial Might to replace Zhou Yu in command of troops, and had Cheng Pu serve as Grand Administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 魯肅勸權以荊州借劉備，與共拒曹操，權從之。

translations.literal: Lu Su urged Quan to lend Jing province to Liu Bei and join with him to resist Cao Cao; Quan followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su urged Sun Quan to lend Jing province to Liu Bei and join with him in resisting Cao Cao. Sun Quan followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 乃分豫章為番陽郡，分長沙為漢昌郡；

translations.literal: He then divided Yuzhang to form Poyang commandery and divided Changsha to form Hanchang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He then divided Yuzhang to form Poyang commandery and divided Changsha to form Hanchang commandery;

sentences.zh: 復以程普領江夏太守，魯肅為漢昌太守，屯陸口。

translations.literal: again he had Cheng Pu serve as Grand Administrator of Jiangxia, Lu Su as Grand Administrator of Hanchang, stationed at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: again he had Cheng Pu serve as Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and Lu Su as Grand Administrator of Hanchang, stationed at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 初，權謂呂蒙曰：「卿今當塗掌事，不可不學。

translations.literal: Earlier, Quan said to Lü Meng: "You now hold power and manage affairs—you cannot fail to study.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sun Quan said to Lü Meng: "You now hold power and manage affairs—you cannot fail to study.

sentences.zh: 」蒙辭以軍中多務。

translations.literal: " Meng declined on the ground that military affairs were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Meng declined on the ground that military affairs kept him too busy.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「孤豈欲卿治經為博士邪！

translations.literal: Quan said: "Do I wish you to master the classics and become a Erudite!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said: "Do I wish you to master the classics and become a Erudite!

sentences.zh: 但當涉獵，見往事耳。

translations.literal: You need only browse broadly and learn from past events.
translations.idiomatic: You need only browse broadly and learn from past events.

sentences.zh: 卿言多務，孰若孤！

translations.literal: You say you are busy—who is busier than I!
translations.idiomatic: You say you are busy—who is busier than I!

sentences.zh: 孤常讀書，自以為大有所益。

translations.literal: I constantly read books and find them of great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly read books and find them of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 」蒙乃始就學。

translations.literal: " Meng then began to study.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Meng then began to study.

sentences.zh: 及魯肅過尋陽，與蒙論議，大驚曰：「卿今者才略，非復吳下阿蒙！

translations.literal: When Lu Su passed through Xunyang and debated with Meng, he was greatly startled and said: "Your talent and strategy today are no longer the A Meng of Wu below!
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Su passed through Xunyang and debated with Lü Meng, he was greatly startled and said: "Your talent and strategy today are no longer the A Meng of Wu below!

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「士別三日，即更刮目相待，大兄何見事之晚乎！

translations.literal: " Meng said: "When a scholar has been apart three days, he must be viewed with fresh eyes—why are you so late in seeing this, elder brother!
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Meng said: "When a scholar has been apart three days, he must be viewed with fresh eyes—why are you so late in seeing this, elder brother!

sentences.zh: 」肅遂拜蒙母，結友而別。

translations.literal: " Su then bowed to Meng's mother, formed friendship, and took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Su then bowed to Lü Meng's mother, formed a bond of friendship, and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 劉備以從事龐統守耒陽令，在縣不治，免官。

translations.literal: Liu Bei had his aide Pang Tong serve as magistrate of Leiyang; in the county he did not govern well and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had his aide Pang Tong serve as magistrate of Leiyang. In the county he did not govern well and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 魯肅遺備書曰：「龐士元非百里才也。

translations.literal: Lu Su wrote Bei: "Pang Shiyuan is not talent for a hundred-li district.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su wrote to Liu Bei: "Pang Shiyuan is not talent fit for a hundred-li district.

sentences.zh: 使處治中、別駕之任，始當展其驥足耳！

translations.literal: If placed in the posts of Registrar or Vice-Director, only then would he fully extend the hooves of his thoroughbred!
translations.idiomatic: If placed in the posts of Registrar or Vice-Director, only then would he fully extend the hooves of his thoroughbred!

sentences.zh: 」諸葛亮亦言之。

translations.literal: " Zhuge Liang also spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuge Liang also spoke on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 備見統，與善譚，大器之，遂用統為治中，親待亞於諸葛亮，與亮並為軍師中郎將。

translations.literal: When Bei met Tong he conversed well with him, greatly valued his capacity, and then employed Tong as Registrar, treating him with intimacy second only to Zhuge Liang; he and Liang both served as Military Adviser Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei met Pang Tong he conversed well with him and greatly valued his capacity. He then employed Tong as Registrar, treating him with intimacy second only to Zhuge Liang. Tong and Liang both served as Military Adviser Gentlemen of the Household.

sentences.zh: 初，蒼梧士燮為交趾太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi Xie of Cangwu served as Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shi Xie of Cangwu served as Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史朱符為夷賊所殺，州郡擾亂，燮表其弟壹領合浦太守，䵋領九真太守，武領南海太守。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiao Zhu Fu was killed by barbarian bandits; the province and commanderies were in turmoil. Xie memorialized that his younger brother Yi should hold Hepu, You Jiuzhen, and Wu Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Jiao Zhu Fu was killed by barbarian bandits, and the province and commanderies fell into turmoil. Xie memorialized that his younger brother Yi should hold Hepu, You Jiuzhen, and Wu Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 燮體器寬厚，中國人士多往依之。

translations.literal: Xie's bearing was generous and thick; many men of the central lands went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie's bearing was generous and magnanimous, and many men of the central lands went to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 雄長一州，偏在萬里，威尊無上，出入儀衛甚盛，震服百蠻。

translations.literal: Dominant over a whole province, remote at ten thousand li, his authority supreme, his guards and escort exceedingly grand—he awed and submitted the hundred barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Dominant over a whole province, remote ten thousand li away, his authority supreme, his guards and escort exceedingly grand—he awed and submitted the hundred barbarian peoples.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣南陽張津為交州刺史。

translations.literal: The court sent Zhang Jin of Nanyang as Inspector of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Zhang Jin of Nanyang as Inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 津好鬼神事，常著絳帕頭，鼓琴、燒香，讀道書，云可以助化，為其將區景所殺。

translations.literal: Jin was fond of spirit matters; he constantly wore a crimson headcloth, played the zither, burned incense, and read Daoist books, saying these could aid transformation—he was killed by his general Qu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was fond of spirit matters. He constantly wore a crimson headcloth, played the zither, burned incense, and read Daoist books, saying these could aid transformation. He was killed by his general Qu Jing.

sentences.zh: 劉表遣零陵賴恭代津為刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Biao sent Lai Gong of Lingling to replace Jin as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sent Lai Gong of Lingling to replace Jin as inspector.

sentences.zh: 是時蒼梧太守史璜死，表又遣吳巨代之。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Administrator of Cangwu Shi Huang died; Biao also sent Wu Ju to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Grand Administrator of Cangwu Shi Huang died. Liu Biao also sent Wu Ju to replace him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賜燮璽書，以燮為綏南中郎將，董督七郡，領交趾太守如故。

translations.literal: The court bestowed on Xie an imperial letter with the seal, making him General Who Pacifies the South and Superintendent of seven commanderies, holding the post of Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court bestowed on Shi Xie an imperial letter with the seal, making him General Who Pacifies the South and Superintendent of seven commanderies, holding the post of Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi as before.

sentences.zh: 後巨與恭相失，巨舉兵逐恭，恭走還零陵。

translations.literal: Later Ju and Gong fell out; Ju raised troops and drove Gong away, and Gong fled back to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Ju and Lai Gong fell out. Ju raised troops and drove Gong away, and Gong fled back to Lingling.

sentences.zh: 孫權以番陽太守臨淮步騭為交州刺史，士燮率兄弟奉承節度。

translations.literal: Sun Quan made Bu Zhi of Linhuai, Grand Administrator of Poyang, Inspector of Jiao; Shi Xie and his brothers led their following to accept his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan made Bu Zhi of Linhuai, Grand Administrator of Poyang, Inspector of Jiao. Shi Xie and his brothers led their following to accept his authority.

sentences.zh: 吳巨外附內違，騭誘而斬之，威聲大震。

translations.literal: Wu Ju was outwardly submissive but inwardly rebellious; Zhi lured and executed him, and his prestige shook the region greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ju was outwardly submissive but inwardly rebellious. Bu Zhi lured and executed him, and his prestige shook the region greatly.

sentences.zh: 權加燮左將軍，燮遣子入質。

translations.literal: Quan promoted Xie to General of the Left; Xie sent his son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan promoted Shi Xie to General of the Left, and Xie sent his son as hostage.

sentences.zh: 由是嶺南始服屬於權。

translations.literal: From this the lands south of the ranges first submitted to Quan's rule.
translations.idiomatic: From this the lands south of the ranges first submitted to Sun Quan's rule.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝辛建安十六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [xin], sixteenth year of Jian'an (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han, sixteenth year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 辛卯，公元二一一年）

translations.literal: xinmao, AD 211)
translations.idiomatic: xinmao, AD 211)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以曹操世子丕為五官中郎將，置官屬，為丞相副。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Cao Cao's heir Pi was made General of the Five Offices and given staff, serving as the Chancellor's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Cao Cao's heir Pi was made General of the Five Offices and given staff, serving as the chancellor's deputy.

sentences.zh: 三月，操遣司隸校尉鐘繇討張魯，使征西護軍夏侯淵等將兵出河東，與繇會。

translations.literal: Third month, Cao sent Minister of Works Zhong Yao to attack Zhang Lu, and had the Protector of the West Xiahou Yuan and others lead troops out of Hedong to join Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Cao Cao sent Minister of Works Zhong Yao to attack Zhang Lu and had the Protector of the West Xiahou Yuan and others lead troops out of Hedong to join Yao.

sentences.zh: 倉曹屬高柔諫曰：「大兵西出，韓遂、馬超疑為襲己，必相扇動。

translations.literal: Gao Rou, an aide in the Granaries Bureau, remonstrated: "When a great army marches west, Han Sui and Ma Chao will suspect it is aimed at them and are sure to stir each other up.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou, an aide in the Granaries Bureau, remonstrated: "When a great army marches west, Han Sui and Ma Chao will suspect it is aimed at them and are sure to stir each other up.

sentences.zh: 宜先招集三輔，三輔苟平，漢中可傳檄而定也。

translations.literal: You should first win over the Three Adjuncts; if the Three Adjuncts are pacified, Hanzhong can be secured by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: You should first win over the Three Adjuncts. If the Three Adjuncts are pacified, Hanzhong can be secured by proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 」操不從。

translations.literal: " Cao did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao did not follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 關中諸將果疑之，馬超、韓遂、侯選、程銀、楊秋、李堪、張橫、梁興、成宜、馬玩等十部皆反，其眾十萬，屯據潼關；

translations.literal: The generals of Guanzhong indeed became suspicious; Ma Chao, Han Sui, Hou Xuan, Cheng Yin, Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Zhang Heng, Liang Xing, Cheng Yi, Ma Wan, and ten divisions all rebelled, their forces numbering one hundred thousand, encamped and holding Tong Pass;
translations.idiomatic: The generals of Guanzhong indeed became suspicious. Ma Chao, Han Sui, Hou Xuan, Cheng Yin, Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Zhang Heng, Liang Xing, Cheng Yi, Ma Wan, and ten divisions all rebelled. Their forces numbered one hundred thousand and encamped at Tong Pass;

sentences.zh: 操遺安西將軍曹仁督諸將拒之，敕令堅壁勿與戰。

translations.literal: Cao sent the Pacifying West General Cao Ren to supervise the generals in resisting them and ordered them to hold their walls and not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent the Pacifying West General Cao Ren to supervise the generals in resisting them and ordered them to hold their walls and not give battle.

sentences.zh: 命五官將丕留守鄴，以奮武將軍程昱參丕軍事，門下督廣陵徐宣為左護軍，留統諸軍，樂安國淵為居府長史，統留事。

translations.literal: He had the General of the Five Offices Pi remain at Ye, with the Martially Resolute General Cheng Yu assisting Pi in military affairs; the Gate Attendant Xu Xuan of Guangling as Left Protector of the Army, remaining to command all forces; Yue An of Guo as Director of the Residence, managing remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had the General of the Five Offices Pi remain at Ye, with the Martially Resolute General Cheng Yu assisting Pi in military affairs; the Gate Attendant Xu Xuan of Guangling as Left Protector of the Army, remaining to command all forces; and Yue An of Guo as Director of the Residence, managing remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，操自將擊超等。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Cao personally led the attack on Chao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, Cao Cao personally led the attack on Ma Chao and the others.

sentences.zh: 議者多言：「關西兵習長矛，非精選前鋒，不可當也。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated mostly said: "The soldiers of Guanxi are skilled with long spears; unless the vanguard is carefully chosen, they cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberated mostly said: "The soldiers of Guanxi are skilled with long spears. Unless the vanguard is carefully chosen, they cannot be withstood.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「戰在我，非在賊也。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Victory in battle lies with me, not with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said: "Victory in battle lies with me, not with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊雖習長矛，將使不得以刺，諸君但觀之。

translations.literal: Though the enemy is skilled with long spears, I will make them unable to thrust—just watch.
translations.idiomatic: Though the enemy is skilled with long spears, I will make them unable to thrust—just watch.

sentences.zh: 八月，操至潼關，與超等夾關而軍。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Cao reached Tong Pass and faced Chao and the others across the pass in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Cao Cao reached Tong Pass and faced Ma Chao and the others across the pass in camp.

sentences.zh: 操急持之，而潛遣徐晃、朱靈以步騎四千人渡浦阪津，據河西為營。

translations.literal: Cao held them in check while secretly sending Xu Huang and Zhu Ling with four thousand infantry and cavalry to cross Puban Ford and encamp on the west bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao held them in check while secretly sending Xu Huang and Zhu Ling with four thousand infantry and cavalry to cross Puban Ford and encamp on the west bank of the river.

sentences.zh: 閏月，操自潼關北渡河。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Cao crossed the river north from Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Cao Cao crossed the river north from Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 兵眾先渡，操獨與虎士百餘人留南岸斷後。

translations.literal: The troops crossed first; Cao alone with a hundred-odd Tiger Guards remained on the south bank as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: The troops crossed first. Cao Cao alone, with a hundred-odd Tiger Guards, remained on the south bank as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 馬超將步騎萬餘人攻之，矢下如雨，操猶據胡床不動。

translations.literal: Ma Chao led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack; arrows fell like rain, yet Cao still sat on his folding camp-chair without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack. Arrows fell like rain, yet Cao Cao still sat on his folding camp-chair without moving.

sentences.zh: 許褚扶操上船，船工中流矢死，褚左手舉馬鞍以蔽操，右手刺船。

translations.literal: Xu Chu helped Cao aboard the boat; the boatman was killed midstream by an arrow. Chu raised a saddle with his left hand to shield Cao and stabbed the boat forward with his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chu helped Cao Cao aboard the boat. The boatman was killed midstream by an arrow. Chu raised a saddle with his left hand to shield Cao and stabbed the boat forward with his right hand.

sentences.zh: 校尉丁斐，放牛馬以餌賊，賊亂取牛馬，操乃得渡。

translations.literal: Colonel Ding Fei released cattle and horses to bait the enemy; the enemy in disorder seized the cattle and horses, and Cao was then able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Ding Fei released cattle and horses to bait the enemy. The enemy in disorder seized the cattle and horses, and Cao Cao was then able to cross.

sentences.zh: 遂自蒲阪渡西河，循河為甬道而南。

translations.literal: He then crossed from Puban to the west bank of the Yellow River and followed the river south along a covered military road.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed from Puban to the west bank of the Yellow River and followed the river south along a covered military road.

sentences.zh: 超等退拒渭口，操乃多設疑兵，潛以舟載兵入渭，為浮橋，夜，分兵結營於渭南。

translations.literal: Chao and the others retreated to hold the mouth of the Wei; Cao set up many dummy forces and secretly ferried troops into the Wei by boat, building a floating bridge. By night he divided troops and encamped south of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao and the others retreated to hold the mouth of the Wei. Cao Cao set up many dummy forces and secretly ferried troops into the Wei by boat, building a floating bridge. By night he divided troops and encamped south of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 超等夜攻營，伏兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Chao and the others attacked the camp by night; ambush troops struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao and the others attacked the camp by night. Ambush troops struck and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 超等屯渭南，遣信求割河以西請和，操不許。

translations.literal: Chao and the others encamped at Weinan and sent envoys asking to cede the lands west of the river and sue for peace; Cao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao and the others encamped at Weinan and sent envoys asking to cede the lands west of the river and sue for peace. Cao Cao would not agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，操進軍，悉渡渭。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Cao advanced his army and crossed the Wei in full.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Cao Cao advanced his army and crossed the Wei in full.

sentences.zh: 超等數挑戰，又不許；

translations.literal: Chao and the others repeatedly challenged to battle, and he would not allow it;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao and the others repeatedly challenged to battle, and he would not allow it;

sentences.zh: 固請割地，求送任子。

translations.literal: they firmly asked to cede territory and offered to send hostages.
translations.idiomatic: they firmly asked to cede territory and offered to send hostages.

sentences.zh: 賈詡以為可偽許之。

translations.literal: Jia Xu thought they could be falsely promised.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu thought they could be falsely promised.

sentences.zh: 操復問計策，詡曰：「離之而已。

translations.literal: Cao again asked for stratagems; Xu said: "Simply divide them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao again asked for stratagems. Xu said: "Simply divide them.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「解！

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Understood!
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said: "Understood!

sentences.zh: 」韓遂請與操相見，操與遂有舊，於是交馬語移時，不及軍事，但說京都舊故，拊手歡笑。

translations.literal: " Han Sui asked to meet with Cao; Cao and Sui had old ties, and so they exchanged horses and spoke for a long while, not touching on military affairs but only recalling old affairs of the capital, clapping hands and laughing.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Sui asked to meet with Cao Cao. Cao and Sui had old ties, and so they exchanged horses and spoke for a long while, not touching on military affairs but only recalling old affairs of the capital, clapping hands and laughing.

sentences.zh: 時秦、胡觀者，前後重沓，操笑謂之曰：「爾欲觀曹公邪！

translations.literal: At that time Qin and Hu onlookers, layer upon layer before and behind; Cao laughed and said to them: "Do you wish to see Lord Cao!
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin and Hu onlookers stood layer upon layer before and behind. Cao Cao laughed and said to them: "Do you wish to see Lord Cao!

sentences.zh: 亦猶人也，非有四目兩口，但多智耳！

translations.literal: He too is a man, without four eyes and two mouths—only more wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: He too is a man, without four eyes and two mouths—only more wisdom!

sentences.zh: 」既罷，超等問遂：「公何言！

translations.literal: " When it ended, Chao and the others asked Sui: "What did he say!
translations.idiomatic: " When it ended, Ma Chao and the others asked Sui: "What did he say!

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「無所言也。

translations.literal: " Sui said: "Nothing was said.
translations.idiomatic: " Sui said: "Nothing was said.

sentences.zh: 」超等疑之。

translations.literal: " Chao and the others grew suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Chao and the others grew suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 他日，操又與遂書，多所點竄，如遂改定者；

translations.literal: Another day, Cao again wrote Sui a letter with many marks and alterations, as if Sui had revised it;
translations.idiomatic: Another day, Cao Cao again wrote Sui a letter with many marks and alterations, as if Sui had revised it;

sentences.zh: 超等愈疑遂。

translations.literal: Chao and the others grew ever more suspicious of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao and the others grew ever more suspicious of Sui.

sentences.zh: 操乃與剋日會戰，先以輕兵挑之，戰良久，乃縱虎騎夾擊，大破之，斬成宜、李堪等。

translations.literal: Cao then joined battle on a set day; first he provoked them with light troops, and after fighting long he unleashed the Tiger Cavalry to strike from both sides, routing them greatly and beheading Cheng Yi, Li Kan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then joined battle on a set day. First he provoked them with light troops, and after fighting long he unleashed the Tiger Cavalry to strike from both sides, routing them greatly and beheading Cheng Yi, Li Kan, and others.

sentences.zh: 遂、超奔涼州，楊秋奔安定。

translations.literal: Sui and Chao fled to Liang province; Yang Qiu fled to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui and Ma Chao fled to Liang province. Yang Qiu fled to Anding.

sentences.zh: 諸將問操曰：「初，賊守潼關，渭北道缺，不從河東擊馮翊而反守潼關，引日而後北渡，何也？

translations.literal: The generals asked Cao: "At first the enemy held Tong Pass and the road north of the Wei was cut off; why did you not attack Fengyi from Hedong but instead held Tong Pass, drawing out days before crossing north—why?
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked Cao Cao: "At first the enemy held Tong Pass and the road north of the Wei was cut off. Why did you not attack Fengyi from Hedong but instead held Tong Pass, drawing out days before crossing north—why?

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「賊守潼關，若吾入河東，賊必引守諸津，則西河未可渡，吾故盛兵向潼關；

translations.literal: " Cao said: "The enemy held Tong Pass; if I entered Hedong, the enemy would surely draw troops to guard every ford, and then the west bank could not be crossed. I therefore massed troops toward Tong Pass;
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said: "The enemy held Tong Pass. If I entered Hedong, the enemy would surely draw troops to guard every ford, and then the west bank could not be crossed. I therefore massed troops toward Tong Pass;

sentences.zh: 賊悉眾南守，西河之備虛，故二將得擅取西河；

translations.literal: the enemy mustered all their forces to guard south, and the west-bank defenses were empty—therefore the two generals could seize the west bank at will;
translations.idiomatic: the enemy mustered all their forces to guard south, and the west-bank defenses were empty—therefore the two generals could seize the west bank at will;

sentences.zh: 然後引軍北渡。

translations.literal: then I led the army north across.
translations.idiomatic: then I led the army north across.

sentences.zh: 賊不能與吾爭西河者，以二將之軍也。

translations.literal: The reason the enemy could not contend with me for the west bank was because of the army of those two generals.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the enemy could not contend with me for the west bank was because of the army of those two generals.

sentences.zh: 連車樹柵，為甬道而南，既為不可勝，且以示弱。

translations.literal: Linking wagons and planting palisades, building the covered road south—this was both to make us unconquerable and to show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Linking wagons and planting palisades, building the covered road south—this was both to make us unconquerable and to show weakness.

sentences.zh: 渡渭為堅壘，虜至不出，所以驕之也；

translations.literal: Crossing the Wei we built stout ramparts; when the barbarians came we did not sally forth—this was to make them arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Wei we built stout ramparts. When the barbarians came we did not sally forth—this was to make them arrogant;

sentences.zh: 故賊不為營壘而求割地。

translations.literal: therefore the enemy did not build ramparts but sought to cede land.
translations.idiomatic: therefore the enemy did not build ramparts but sought to cede land.

sentences.zh: 吾順言許之，所以從其意，使自安而不為備，因畜士卒之力，一旦擊之，所謂疾雷不及掩耳。

translations.literal: I agreed in words to promise them—this was to follow their intent, let them grow secure and make no preparations, while storing up the strength of the troops; then in one strike—what is called thunder too swift for the ear to cover."
translations.idiomatic: I agreed in words to promise them—this was to follow their intent, let them grow secure and make no preparations, while storing up the strength of the troops. Then in one strike—what is called thunder too swift for the ear to cover."

sentences.zh: 兵之變化，固非一道也。

translations.literal: The transformations of warfare are certainly not of one pattern alone.
translations.idiomatic: The transformations of warfare are certainly not of one pattern alone.

sentences.zh: 始，關中諸將每一部到，操輒有喜色。

translations.literal: At the start, whenever one division of the Guanzhong generals arrived, Cao would show pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At the start, whenever one division of the Guanzhong generals arrived, Cao Cao would show pleasure.

sentences.zh: 諸將問其故，操曰：「關中長遠，若賊各依險阻，征之，不一二年不可定也。

translations.literal: The generals asked the reason; Cao said: "Guanzhong is far and broad; if the enemy each relied on perilous terrain, to campaign against them would take no less than a year or two to settle.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked the reason. Cao said: "Guanzhong is far and broad. If the enemy each relied on perilous terrain, to campaign against them would take no less than a year or two to settle.

sentences.zh: 今皆來集，其眾雖多，莫相歸服，軍無適主，一舉可滅，為功差易，吾是以喜。

translations.literal: Now they have all come together; though their numbers are many, none defer to another as leader—the army has no proper commander. One stroke can destroy them; the achievement is rather easier. That is why I am pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have all come together. Though their numbers are many, none defer to another as leader—the army has no proper commander. One stroke can destroy them. The achievement is rather easier. That is why I am pleased.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，操自長安北征楊秋，圍安定。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Cao marched north from Chang'an to campaign against Yang Qiu and besieged Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, Cao Cao marched north from Chang'an to campaign against Yang Qiu and besieged Anding.

sentences.zh: 秋降，復其爵位，使留撫其民。

translations.literal: Qiu surrendered; Cao restored his noble rank and fief and had him remain to pacify his people.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu surrendered. Cao Cao restored his noble rank and fief and had him remain to pacify his people.

sentences.zh: 十二月，操自安定還，留夏侯淵屯長安。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Cao returned from Anding and left Xiahou Yuan stationed at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Cao Cao returned from Anding and left Xiahou Yuan stationed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以議郎張既為京兆尹。

translations.literal: He appointed Imperial Counsellor Zhang Ji as Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao appointed Zhang Ji, an Imperial Counsellor, as Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 既招懷流民，興復縣邑，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: Ji summoned and comforted displaced people, restored counties and towns, and the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji summoned and comforted displaced people, restored the counties and towns, and the people came to love him.

sentences.zh: 遂、超之叛也，弘農、馮翊縣邑多應之，河東民獨無異心。

translations.literal: When Sui and Chao rebelled, many counties and towns in Hongnong and Fufeng responded; only the people of Hedong had no divergent hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui and Ma Chao rebelled, many counties and towns in Hongnong and Fufeng joined them, but the people of Hedong alone showed no disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 操與超等夾渭為軍，軍食一仰河東。

translations.literal: Cao and Chao and the others encamped on both sides of the Wei River; army provisions entirely depended on Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao and Ma Chao and the others encamped on opposite banks of the Wei River, and all military provisions came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 及超等破，餘畜尚二十餘萬斛，操乃增河東太守杜畿秩中二千石。

translations.literal: When Chao and the others were defeated, surplus stored grain still exceeded two hundred thousand hu; Cao then promoted Hedong Administrator Du Ji to rank of middle two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Chao and the others were defeated, more than two hundred thousand hu of grain remained in storage, and Cao Cao promoted Hedong Administrator Du Ji to the rank of middle two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 扶風法正為劉璋軍議校尉，璋不能用，又為其州裡俱僑客者所鄙，正邑邑不得志。

translations.literal: Fufeng's Fa Zheng served as Military Adviser Colonel for Liu Zhang, but Zhang could not employ him; moreover he was despised by fellow provincials who were all guest outsiders, and Zheng was depressed and could not realize his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng of Fufeng served Liu Zhang as Military Adviser Colonel, but Liu Zhang failed to make use of him. He was also looked down on by fellow provincials who, like him, were outsiders in the province, and Fa Zheng grew frustrated and despondent.

sentences.zh: 益州別駕張松與正善，自負其才，忖璋不足與有為，常竊歎息。

translations.literal: Yizhou Assistant Commissioner Zhang Song was on good terms with Zheng; relying on his own talent, he reckoned Zhang insufficient for great undertakings and often sighed secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song, Assistant Commissioner of Yizhou, was on good terms with Fa Zheng. Confident in his own abilities, he considered Liu Zhang incapable of great achievements and often sighed in private.

sentences.zh: 松勸璋結劉備，璋曰：「誰可使者？

translations.literal: Song urged Zhang to ally with Liu Bei; Zhang said: "Who can be sent as envoy?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song urged Liu Zhang to ally with Liu Bei. Liu Zhang asked, "Who can be sent as envoy?

sentences.zh: 」松乃舉正。

translations.literal: " Song then recommended Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Song then recommended Fa Zheng.

sentences.zh: 璋使正往，正辭謝，佯為不得已而行。

translations.literal: Zhang sent Zheng to go; Zheng declined, feigning that he went only because he had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang sent Fa Zheng on the mission. Fa Zheng declined at first, then pretended to go only because he had no choice.

sentences.zh: 還，為松說備有雄略，密謀奉戴以為州主。

translations.literal: On returning, he told Song that Bei had heroic strategy, and they secretly plotted to install him as lord of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he told Zhang Song that Liu Bei possessed great strategic vision, and they secretly plotted to install him as ruler of the province.

sentences.zh: 會曹操遣鐘繇向漢中，璋聞之，內懷恐懼。

translations.literal: It happened that Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao toward Hanzhong; when Zhang heard, inwardly he harbored fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao toward Hanzhong. When Liu Zhang heard of it, he was filled with fear.

sentences.zh: 松因說璋曰：「曹公兵無敵於天下，若因張魯之資以取蜀土，誰能御之！

translations.literal: Song then urged Zhang, saying: "Lord Cao's troops are matchless under Heaven; if he uses Zhang Lu's resources to seize Shu territory, who can resist him!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song then urged Liu Zhang, saying, "Lord Cao's armies are unmatched in the realm. If he uses Zhang Lu's resources to seize the lands of Shu, who can stop him!

sentences.zh: 劉豫州，使君之宗室而曹公之深仇也，善用兵。

translations.literal: Liu the Prefect of Yu is your lordship's clansman and Lord Cao's deep enemy; he is skilled at warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei, the Governor of Yu Province, is your clansman and Cao Cao's sworn enemy, and he is skilled in warfare.

sentences.zh: 若使之討魯，魯必破矣。

translations.literal: If you have him attack Lu, Lu will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: If you send him to attack Zhang Lu, Zhang Lu will surely be defeated.

sentences.zh: 魯破，則益州強，曹公雖來，無能為也。

translations.literal: When Lu is broken, then Yizhou will be strong; even if Lord Cao comes, he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Lu is defeated, Yizhou will grow strong, and even if Lord Cao comes, he will be powerless.

sentences.zh: 今州中諸將龐羲、李異等，皆恃功驕豪，欲有外意。

translations.literal: Now among the generals in the province, Pang Xi, Li Yi, and others all rely on merit and are proud and overbearing, desiring to turn outward.
translations.idiomatic: Many generals in the province, such as Pang Xi and Li Yi, have grown arrogant over their achievements and are looking to break away.

sentences.zh: 不得豫州，則敵攻其外，民攻其內，必敗之道也。

translations.literal: If you do not obtain the Prefect of Yu, then enemies will attack from without and the people will attack from within — the path of certain defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Without Liu Bei, you will face enemies without and rebellion within — a path to certain defeat.

sentences.zh: 」璋然之，遣法正將四千人迎備。

translations.literal: " Zhang agreed, and sent Fa Zheng with four thousand men to welcome Bei.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang agreed and sent Fa Zheng with four thousand men to welcome Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 主簿巴西黃權諫曰：「劉左將軍有驍名，今請到，欲以部曲遇之，則不滿其心；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Huang Quan of Baxi remonstrated, saying: "General Liu the Left has a fierce reputation; now that you have invited him, if you treat him as one treats a subordinate officer, you will not satisfy his heart;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan, Chief Clerk of Baxi, remonstrated, saying, "General Liu of the Left enjoys a formidable reputation. Now that you have invited him here, if you treat him as a subordinate commander, you will not win his loyalty;

sentences.zh: 欲以賓客禮待，則一國不容二君，若客有泰山之安，則主有累卵之危。

translations.literal: if you wish to receive him with guest etiquette, then one state cannot contain two lords; if the guest has Mount Tai's stability, then the host has piled-eggs danger.
translations.idiomatic: but if you receive him as an honored guest, one state cannot hold two rulers. If the guest enjoys the security of Mount Tai, the host will face the peril of eggs stacked atop one another.

sentences.zh: 不若閉境以待時清。

translations.literal: Better to close the borders and await the time when order is restored.
translations.idiomatic: Better to seal the borders and wait until the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 」璋不聽，出權為廣漢長。

translations.literal: " Zhang did not listen, and sent Quan out to serve as Prefect of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang refused to listen and reassigned Huang Quan to be Prefect of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 從事廣漢王累，自倒縣於州門以諫，璋一無所訥。

translations.literal: Attendant Wang Lei of Guanghan hung himself upside down at the provincial gate to remonstrate; Zhang did not heed him in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lei, an Attendant of Guanghan, hung himself upside down at the provincial gate to remonstrate, but Liu Zhang paid him no attention whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 法正至荊州，陰獻策於劉備曰：「以明將軍之英才，乘劉牧之之懦弱；

translations.literal: Fa Zheng reached Jingzhou and secretly presented a plan to Liu Bei, saying: "With the bright general's heroic talent, riding upon Governor Liu's weakness;
translations.idiomatic: When Fa Zheng reached Jingzhou, he secretly presented a plan to Liu Bei, saying, "With your brilliant talents, General, and Liu Zhang's weakness to exploit,

sentences.zh: 張松，州之股肱，響應於內；

translations.literal: Zhang Song, the province's right arm, responding from within;
translations.idiomatic: with Zhang Song, the province's trusted pillar, responding from within,

sentences.zh: 以取益州，猶反掌也。

translations.literal: to take Yizhou would be like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: seizing Yizhou would be as easy as turning over your hand.

sentences.zh: 」備疑未決。

translations.literal: " Bei hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 龐統言於備曰：「荊州荒殘，人物殫盡，東有孫車騎，北有曹操，難以得志。

translations.literal: Pang Tong spoke to Bei, saying: "Jingzhou is desolate and ruined, men and talent exhausted; east is Sun the Chariots-and-Horses General, north is Cao Cao — hard to fulfill ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tong said to Liu Bei, "Jingzhou is devastated and its people exhausted. Sun Quan, the General of Chariots and Cavalry, lies to the east and Cao Cao to the north. It will be hard to achieve your ambition here.

sentences.zh: 今益州戶口百萬，土沃財富，誠得以為資，大業可成也！

translations.literal: Now Yizhou has a million households, fertile land and abundant wealth; if you truly obtain it as capital, great enterprise can be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou now has a million households, fertile land, and vast wealth. If you can truly make it your base, you can fulfill your great enterprise!

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「今指與吾為水火者，曹操也。

translations.literal: " Bei said: "Now he whom I point to as my fire and water is Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei said, "The man I count as my mortal enemy is Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操以急，吾以寬；

translations.literal: Cao uses urgency, I use leniency;
translations.idiomatic: He is harsh; I am lenient.

sentences.zh: 操以暴，吾以仁；

translations.literal: Cao uses cruelty, I use benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: He is cruel; I am humane.

sentences.zh: 操以譎，吾以忠。

translations.literal: Cao uses deceit, I use loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He is deceitful; I am honest.

sentences.zh: 每與操反，事乃可成耳。

translations.literal: Each time I oppose Cao, affairs can then succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Only by standing against Cao Cao at every turn can I hope to succeed.

sentences.zh: 今以小利而失信義於天下，奈何？

translations.literal: Now for a small profit to lose faith and righteousness before all under Heaven — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: How can I sacrifice faith and righteousness throughout the realm for a small gain?

sentences.zh: 」統曰：「亂離之時，固非一道所能定也。

translations.literal: " Tong said: "In times of chaos and separation, surely one path alone cannot settle all.
translations.idiomatic: " Pang Tong said, "In an age of chaos and upheaval, no single path can settle everything.

sentences.zh: 且兼弱攻昧，逆取順守，古人所貴。

translations.literal: Moreover, annexing the weak and attacking the dim, taking by force and governing by righteousness — what ancients prized.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to annex the weak and strike the incapable, to seize by force and govern with righteousness — this is what the ancients valued.

sentences.zh: 若事定之後，封以大國，何負於信！

translations.literal: If after affairs are settled you enfeoff him with a great state, how does that betray faith!
translations.idiomatic: Once matters are settled, you can enfeoff him with a great domain. Where is the breach of faith in that?

sentences.zh: 今日不取，終為人利耳。

translations.literal: If today you do not take it, in the end it will serve others' benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not seize it now, someone else will benefit from it in the end.

sentences.zh: 」備以為然。

translations.literal: " Bei deemed it so.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃留諸葛亮、關羽等守荊州，以趙雲領留營司馬，備將步卒數萬人入益州。

translations.literal: He then left Zhuge Liang, Guan Yu, and others to guard Jingzhou, had Zhao Yun lead as Retaining Camp Marshal, and Bei led several tens of thousands of foot soldiers into Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left Zhuge Liang, Guan Yu, and others to guard Jingzhou, appointed Zhao Yun to command the rear camp, and led several tens of thousands of infantry into Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 孫權聞備西上，遣舟船迎妹，而夫人欲將備子禪還吳，張飛、趙雲勒兵截江，乃得禪還。

translations.literal: Sun Quan heard Bei was going west and sent boats to welcome his sister; the lady wished to take Bei's son Shan back to Wu, but Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun deployed troops to block the river and only then obtained Shan's return.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan heard that Liu Bei was marching west, he sent ships to fetch his sister. Lady Sun wished to take Liu Bei's son Liu Shan back to Wu, but Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun deployed troops and intercepted the river passage, securing the boy's return.

sentences.zh: 劉璋敕在所供奉備，備入境如歸，前後贈遺以巨億計。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang ordered that everywhere Bei be supplied; when Bei entered the territory it was like returning home, and gifts before and after totaled hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang ordered that Liu Bei be provisioned wherever he went. Liu Bei entered the province as if returning home, and gifts amounting to hundreds of millions were lavished upon him.

sentences.zh: 備至巴郡，巴郡太守嚴顏拊心歎曰：「此所謂『獨坐窮山，放虎自衛』者也。

translations.literal: When Bei reached Bajiun, Bajiun Administrator Yan Yan clapped his heart and sighed: "This is what is called 'sitting alone in barren mountains, releasing a tiger to guard oneself.'
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei reached Bajiun, its prefect Yan Yan beat his breast and sighed, "This is what people call 'sitting alone on a desolate mountain and letting loose a tiger to guard yourself.'

sentences.zh: 」備自江州北由墊江水詣涪。

translations.literal: " Bei from Jiangzhou went north along the Dian River water route to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei traveled north from Jiangzhou along the Dian River to Fu.

sentences.zh: 璋率步騎三萬餘人，車乘帳幔，精光耀日，往會之。

translations.literal: Zhang led more than thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, chariots, curtains, and banners whose brilliance dazzled the sun, going to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang led more than thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, with chariots, tents, and banners gleaming in the sun, to meet him.

sentences.zh: 張松令法正白備，便於會襲璋。

translations.literal: Zhang Song had Fa Zheng inform Bei that at the meeting he should seize Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song had Fa Zheng tell Liu Bei to seize Liu Zhang at the meeting.

sentences.zh: 備曰：「此事不可倉猝！

translations.literal: Bei said: "This matter cannot be done in haste!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said, "This cannot be done in haste!

sentences.zh: 」龐統曰：「今因會執之，則將軍無用兵之勞而坐定一州也。

translations.literal: " Pang Tong said: "Now by seizing him at the meeting, the general would have no labor of warfare yet sit and settle a whole province.
translations.idiomatic: " Pang Tong said, "If you seize him at this meeting, General, you can secure an entire province without the hardship of campaigning.

sentences.zh: 」備曰：「初入他國，恩信未著，此不可也。

translations.literal: " Bei said: "Just entering another state, grace and faith not yet established — this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei said, "I have only just entered another man's territory, and my goodwill is not yet established. This cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」璋推備行大司馬，領司隸校尉；

translations.literal: " Zhang promoted Bei to act as Grand Marshal and supervise as Colonel Director of Retainers;
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang had Liu Bei act as Grand Marshal and serve as Colonel Director of Retainers;

sentences.zh: 備亦推璋行鎮西大將軍，領益州牧。

translations.literal: Bei also promoted Zhang to act as Great General Who Pacifies the West and supervise as Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei in turn had Liu Zhang act as Great General Who Pacifies the West and serve as Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 所將將士，更相之適，歡飲百餘日。

translations.literal: The generals and soldiers they led paid mutual visits, feasting and drinking for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Their officers and men visited one another in turn and feasted together for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 璋增備兵，厚加資給，使擊張魯，又令督白水軍。

translations.literal: Zhang increased Bei's troops, richly added supplies, had him attack Zhang Lu, and also ordered him to supervise the White Water army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang reinforced Liu Bei's troops, supplied him generously, and sent him to attack Zhang Lu, also assigning him to command the White Water garrison.

sentences.zh: 備並軍三萬餘人，車甲、器械、資貨甚盛。

translations.literal: Bei combined armies totaling more than thirty thousand men, with chariots, armor, weapons, and goods very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's combined force numbered more than thirty thousand men, with chariots, armor, weapons, and supplies in great abundance.

sentences.zh: 璋還成教，備北到葭萌，未即討魯，厚樹恩德以收眾心。

translations.literal: Zhang returned to Chengdu; Bei went north to Jiameng, did not immediately attack Lu, and richly planted benevolence and virtue to win the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang returned to Chengdu. Liu Bei marched north to Jiameng but did not immediately attack Zhang Lu, instead cultivating goodwill to win over the people.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝辛建安十七年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [xin], seventeenth year of Jian'an (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han, seventeenth year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 壬辰，公元二一二年）

translations.literal: rensi, AD 212)
translations.idiomatic: the day rensi, AD 212)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曹操還鄴。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Cao Cao returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Cao Cao returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔操贊拜不名，入朝不趨，劍履上殿，如蕭何故事。

translations.literal: An edict granted Cao the privilege that his name need not be spoken in full when praised, that he need not hasten when entering court, and that he might enter the hall wearing sword and shoes — as in Xiao He's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Cao Cao the privileges of having his name spoken in abbreviated form at court, entering audience without hurrying, and wearing sword and shoes in the imperial hall, following the precedent set for Xiao He.

sentences.zh: 操之西征也，河間民田銀、蘇伯反，扇動幽、冀。

translations.literal: When Cao was on his western campaign, the people of Hejian Tian Yin and Su Bo rebelled, stirring up You and Ji.
