translations.idiomatic: During Cao Cao's western campaign, Tian Yin and Su Bo of Hejian rebelled and stirred up trouble in You and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 五官將丕欲自討之，功曹常林曰：「北方吏民，樂安厭亂，服化已久，守善者多；

translations.literal: General of the Five Offices Pi wished to campaign against them himself; Records Officer Chang Lin said: "Northern officials and people delight in peace and loathe chaos; they have submitted to civilization long, and many keep to goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Pi, the General of the Five Offices, wished to lead the campaign himself. Chang Lin, the Records Officer, said, "The officials and people of the north delight in peace and loathe disorder. They have been civilized for a long time, and most abide by the law;

sentences.zh: 銀、伯犬羊相聚，不能為害。

translations.literal: Yin and Bo are dogs and sheep gathered together — they cannot do harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Bo are a rabble scarcely better than dogs and sheep. They cannot do much harm.

sentences.zh: 方今大軍在遠，外有強敵，將軍為天下之鎮，輕運遠舉，雖克不武。

translations.literal: Now the great army is far away, outside are strong enemies; the general is the realm's anchor — a light expedition far afield, even if victorious, is not martially prudent.
translations.idiomatic: The main army is far away, and strong enemies remain abroad. You, General, are the anchor of the realm. To make a distant expedition on a whim would be imprudent even if you won.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣將軍賈信討之，應時克滅。

translations.literal: " So he sent General Jia Xin to suppress them, and they were destroyed on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " So he sent General Jia Xin to suppress them, and the rebels were destroyed at once.

sentences.zh: 餘賊千餘人請降，議者皆曰：「公有舊法，圍而後降者不赦。

translations.literal: More than a thousand remaining rebels requested surrender; those in council all said: "The lord has an old law — those who surrender only after being surrounded are not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand surviving rebels asked to surrender. The advisers all said, "My lord has an old rule: those who surrender only after being surrounded are not to be spared.

sentences.zh: 」程昱曰：「此乃擾攘之際，權時之宜。

translations.literal: " Cheng Yu said: "This was a measure for turbulent times, a provisional expedient.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Yu said, "That rule was meant for turbulent times — a provisional expedient.

sentences.zh: 今天下略定，不可誅之；

translations.literal: Now the realm is largely settled; they must not be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is largely pacified. They must not be executed.

sentences.zh: 縱誅之，宜先啟聞。

translations.literal: even if they were to be executed, one should first report and ask permission.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they were to be executed, you should first report to Lord Cao and obtain his approval.

sentences.zh: 」議者皆曰：「軍事有專無請。

translations.literal: " Those in council all said: "In military affairs there is sole authority without asking.
translations.idiomatic: " The advisers replied, "In military affairs one has sole authority and need not ask permission.

sentences.zh: 」昱曰：「凡專命者，謂有臨時之急耳。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Sole authority in all cases refers only to urgent circumstances on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Yu said, "Sole authority applies only when urgent circumstances leave no time to ask.

sentences.zh: 今此賊制在賈信之手，故老臣不願將軍行之也。

translations.literal: Now these rebels are controlled in Jia Xin's hands — therefore this old minister does not wish the general to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: These rebels are now in Jia Xin's hands. That is why I, an old minister, would rather you not carry out the executions yourself, General.

sentences.zh: 」丕曰：「善。

translations.literal: " Pi said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi said, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 」即白操，操果不誅。

translations.literal: " He immediately reported to Cao, and Cao indeed did not execute them.
translations.idiomatic: " He reported to Cao Cao at once, and Cao Cao indeed did not execute them.

sentences.zh: 既而聞昱之謀，甚悅，曰：「君非徒明於軍計，又善處人父子之間。

translations.literal: Later when he heard Yu's counsel, he was greatly pleased and said: "You are not only clear in military planning, but also skilled in handling relations between men and fathers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao later heard of Cheng Yu's advice, he was greatly pleased and said, "You understand military strategy, and you also know how to handle matters between a father and his son.

sentences.zh: 」故事：破賊文書，以一為十。

translations.literal: " Precedent: in reports of defeating bandits, one was counted as ten.
translations.idiomatic: " By custom, reports of defeating bandits inflated the count tenfold.

sentences.zh: 國淵上首級，皆如其實數，操問其故，淵曰：「夫征討外寇，多其斬獲之數者，欲以大武功，聳民聽也。

translations.literal: Guo Yuan submitted head counts all matching actual numbers; Cao asked the reason; Yuan said: "When campaigning against external bandits, inflating the number slain and captured is to magnify martial achievements and startle the people's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan reported head counts that matched the actual numbers. When Cao Cao asked why, Guo Yuan said, "When campaigning against foreign enemies, inflating the number of kills is meant to magnify military achievement and impress the people.

sentences.zh: 河間在封域之內，銀等叛逆，雖克捷有功，淵竊恥之。

translations.literal: Hejian is within the sealed domain; Yin and the others rebelled — though victory had merit, Yuan personally felt shame at it.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian lies within our own territory. When Yin and the others rebelled, victory brought little honor. I would be ashamed to inflate the count.

sentences.zh: 」操大悅。

translations.literal: " Cao was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，癸未，誅衛尉馬騰，夷三族。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day guiwei, executed Commandant of Guards Ma Teng and exterminated three clans.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on the day guiwei, Ma Teng, Commandant of the Guards, was executed and his clan exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, last day of gengyin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the last day of the gengyin cycle, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，螟。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, locust larvae.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, locust larvae ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 馬超等餘眾頓藍田，夏侯淵擊平之。

translations.literal: Ma Chao and others' remaining host encamped at Lantian; Xiahou Yuan attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining followers of Ma Chao and others were encamped at Lantian. Xiahou Yuan attacked and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 鄜賊梁興寇略馮翊，諸縣恐懼，皆寄治郡下，議者以為當移就險阻。

translations.literal: Liang Xing the bandit of Fu raided and plundered Fufeng; all counties were afraid and all administered from below the commandery seat; those in council thought they should move to perilous strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Liang Xing of Fu raided Fufeng. Fearful, the counties all relocated their administrations to the commandery seat, and the advisers thought they should withdraw to defensible terrain.

sentences.zh: 左馮翊鄭渾曰：「興等破散，藏竄山谷，雖有隨者，率脅從耳。

translations.literal: Left Administrator of Fufeng Zheng Hun said: "Xing and the others are broken and scattered, hiding in mountain valleys; though some follow them, mostly they are coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hun, Left Administrator of Fufeng, said, "Xing and the others are broken and scattered, hiding in the mountains. Those who follow them are mostly coerced.

sentences.zh: 今當廣開降路，宣喻威信。

translations.literal: Now we should widely open the path of surrender and proclaim authority and trust.
translations.idiomatic: We should now open wide the path to surrender and make our authority and good faith known.

sentences.zh: 而保險自守，此示弱也。

translations.literal: Yet to hold perilous positions and defend ourselves — this shows weakness.
translations.idiomatic: To hold defensible ground and hide behind walls would only show weakness.

sentences.zh: 」乃聚吏民，治城郭，為守備，募民逐賊，得其財物婦女，十以七賞。

translations.literal: " He then gathered officials and people, repaired walls, made defenses, recruited people to pursue bandits, and granted seven-tenths of goods and women captured to them.
translations.idiomatic: " He gathered the officials and people, repaired the city walls, prepared defenses, and recruited civilians to hunt the bandits, granting them seven-tenths of any goods or captives seized.

sentences.zh: 民大悅，皆願捕賊；

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased and all wished to capture bandits;
translations.idiomatic: The people were greatly pleased and all volunteered to hunt the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊之失妻子者皆還，求降，渾責其得他婦女，然後還之。

translations.literal: Bandits who had lost wives and children all returned and sought to surrender; Hun held those who had taken others' women accountable, then returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits who had lost their wives and children came back seeking to surrender. Zheng Hun forced those who had taken other men's women to return them before he would accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是轉相寇盜，黨與離散。

translations.literal: Thereupon they turned to robbing one another, and factions dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then began raiding one another, and their factions broke apart.

sentences.zh: 又遣吏民有恩信者分佈山谷告諭之，出者相繼。

translations.literal: He also sent officials and people of trust to spread through mountain valleys and instruct them; those who came out followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent trusted officials and civilians into the mountains to proclaim his message, and surrendering bandits emerged in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 乃使諸縣長吏各還本治，以安集之。

translations.literal: He then had each county's chief officials all return to their original jurisdictions to settle and gather the people.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the county magistrates back to their original posts to reassure and resettle the people.

sentences.zh: 興等懼，將餘從聚鄜城。

translations.literal: Xing and the others grew afraid and gathered their remaining followers at Fu city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xing and the others, now afraid, gathered their remaining followers at Fu city.

sentences.zh: 操使夏侯淵助渾討之，遂斬興，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Cao had Xiahou Yuan assist Hun in suppressing them, then beheaded Xing, and the remaining party was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan to assist Zheng Hun in the campaign. Liang Xing was beheaded, and the remaining rebels were completely suppressed.

sentences.zh: 渾，泰之弟也。

translations.literal: Hun was Tai's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hun was the younger brother of Zheng Tai.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚戌，立皇子熙為濟陰王，懿為山陽王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day gengxu, established Imperial Son Xi as King of Jiyin and Yi as King of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day gengxu, Imperial Son Cao Xi was made King of Jiyin and Cao Yi King of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 邈為濟北王，敦為東海王。

translations.literal: Miao was made King of Jibei and Dun King of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Miao was made King of Jibei and Cao Dun King of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 初，張紘以秣陵山川形勝，勸孫權以為治所；

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Hong, because Moling's mountains, rivers, and terrain were strategically superior, urged Sun Quan to make it his seat of government;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Hong urged Sun Quan to make Moling his capital on account of its superior terrain and natural defenses;

sentences.zh: 及劉備東過秣陵，亦勸權居之。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei passed east through Moling, he also urged Quan to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei passed east through Moling, he too urged Sun Quan to make it his capital.

sentences.zh: 權於是作石頭城，徙治秣陵，改末陵為建業。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon built Stone City, moved the seat of government to Moling, and changed Moling to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then built Stone City, moved his capital to Moling, and renamed it Jianye.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙聞曹操欲東兵，說孫權夾濡須水口立塢。

translations.literal: Lü Meng heard that Cao Cao intended to march east with troops, and advised Sun Quan to build a fortified camp flanking both sides of the Ruxu river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng learned that Cao Cao planned to march east, he urged Sun Quan to build fortified camps on both banks of the Ruxu river mouth.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「上岸擊賊，洗足入船，何用塢為！

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Going ashore to strike the enemy, washing feet and entering the boat — what use is a fortified camp!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "We go ashore to strike the enemy, wash our feet, and step back into our boats — what do we need a fort for!"

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「兵有利鈍，戰無百勝，如有邂逅，敵步騎蹙人，不暇及水，其得入船乎？

translations.literal: " Meng said: "Weapons have sharp and dull; in battle there is no hundred victories. If there should be an unexpected encounter and the enemy's infantry and cavalry press upon one, with no leisure to reach the water — could one get into the boats?"
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Meng replied, "Weapons have their advantages and disadvantages, and no battle is ever won with certainty. If we meet the enemy unexpectedly and their infantry and cavalry close in, we may not have time to reach the water — how then would we board our ships?"

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Quan said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 」遂作濡須塢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he built the Ruxu fort.
translations.idiomatic: " And so the Ruxu fort was built.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，曹操東擊孫權。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Cao Cao marched east to attack Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Cao Cao marched east to attack Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 董昭言於曹操曰：「自古以來，人臣匡世，未有今日之功；

translations.literal: Dong Zhao spoke to Cao Cao, saying: "Since antiquity, ministers who set the age aright have never had achievements like those of today;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao said to Cao Cao, "Since antiquity, no minister who steered the age through crisis has ever achieved what you have today;

sentences.zh: 有今日之功，未有久處人臣之勢者也。

translations.literal: to have achievements like today's, yet never to have long remained in the position of a minister-subject.
translations.idiomatic: yet to hold such achievements while remaining indefinitely in the position of a subject — that has never happened.

sentences.zh: 今明公恥有慚德，樂保名節。

translations.literal: Now my lord is ashamed of having moral debt and delights in preserving reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: You are ashamed of seeming overambitious and wish to preserve your reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 然處大臣之勢，使人以大事疑己，誠不可不重慮也。

translations.literal: Yet occupying the position of a great minister, causing people to suspect you over great affairs — this truly cannot but be deeply reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet occupying such a powerful position invites suspicion over your ultimate intentions — this is something you must weigh carefully indeed.

sentences.zh: 」乃與列侯諸將議，以丞相宜進爵國公，九錫備物，以彰殊勳。

translations.literal: " He then consulted with marquises and generals that the Chancellor should be advanced to the nobility of State Duke, with the nine bestowals completely supplied, to manifest extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: " Dong Zhao then consulted with the marquises and generals, proposing that the Chancellor be elevated to Duke of a state and granted the full nine insignia of honor to celebrate his extraordinary achievements.

sentences.zh: 荀彧以為：「曹公本興義兵以匡朝寧國，秉忠貞之誠，守退讓之實。

translations.literal: Xun Yu held that: "Lord Cao originally raised righteous troops to set the court aright and pacify the state, holding sincere loyalty and guarding the reality of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu objected, "Lord Cao originally raised righteous troops to restore the dynasty and pacify the realm, holding fast to loyal devotion and the virtue of restraint.

sentences.zh: 君子愛人以德，不宜如此。

translations.literal: A gentleman loves others through virtue; he should not act in this way.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman honors others through virtue — such a move would be unworthy of him.

sentences.zh: 」操由是不悅。

translations.literal: " Cao thereby became displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及擊孫權，表請彧勞軍於譙，因輒留彧，以侍中、光祿大夫、持節、參丞相軍事。

translations.literal: When he attacked Sun Quan, he memorialized requesting Yu to encourage the army at Qiao, and on that pretext detained Yu, appointing him Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Bearer of the Staff, and participant in the Chancellor's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Sun Quan, he submitted a memorial asking Xun Yu to go to Qiao to encourage the troops, then kept him there, appointing him Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, and participant in the Chancellor's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 操軍向濡須，彧以疾留壽春，飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: Cao's army headed toward Ruxu; Yu remained at Shouchun on grounds of illness and died after taking medicine.
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao's army marched toward Ruxu, Xun Yu remained at Shouchun on account of illness and died after drinking poison.

sentences.zh: 彧行義修整而有智謀，好推賢進士，故時人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Yu's conduct in righteousness was orderly and he possessed wisdom and strategy; he loved recommending the worthy and advancing scholars — therefore men of the time all lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu was upright in conduct, gifted with wisdom and strategy, and devoted to recommending worthy men and advancing scholars — for this reason all who knew him mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：孔子之言仁也重矣，自子路、冉求、公西赤門人之高第，令尹子文、陳文子諸侯之賢大夫，皆不足以當之，而獨稱管仲之仁，豈非以其輔佐齊桓，大濟生民乎！

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Confucius's words on benevolence are weighty indeed. From Zilu, Ran Qiu, and Gongxichi — the top disciples among his followers — to Chief Minister Ziwen and Minister Chen Wenzi, worthy grandees among the feudal lords, none sufficed to bear the title, yet he alone praised Guan Zhong's benevolence — was it not because Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan of Qi and greatly succored the living people!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Confucius weighed the word "benevolence" heavily indeed. None of his foremost disciples — Zilu, Ran Qiu, and Gongxichi — nor worthy ministers of the feudal lords, such as Chief Minister Ziwen and Minister Chen Wenzi, was deemed worthy of that praise. Yet Confucius singled out Guan Zhong as benevolent — surely because Guan Zhong served Duke Huan of Qi and brought great relief to the people!

sentences.zh: 齊桓之行若狗彘，管仲不羞而相之，其志蓋以非桓公則生民不可得而濟也，漢末大亂，群生塗炭，自非高世之才不能濟也。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi's conduct was like dogs and pigs; Guan Zhong was not ashamed but served as his chancellor — his intent perhaps was that unless through Duke Huan, the living people could not be succored. At the end of Han came great disorder; the masses were in mud and fire — only talent transcending the age could succor them.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi's conduct was debased as a dog's or a pig's, yet Guan Zhong felt no shame in serving as his chancellor — because he understood that without Duke Huan, the people could not be saved. At the end of the Han dynasty came cataclysmic disorder, and the people suffered as though treading through fire. Only talent of the highest order could deliver them.

sentences.zh: 然則荀彧捨魏武將誰事哉！

translations.literal: In that case, if Xun Yu abandoned Wei Wu, whom would he serve!
translations.idiomatic: In that case, if Xun Yu had abandoned Cao Cao, whom else could he have served?

sentences.zh: 齊桓之時，周室雖衰，未若建安之初也。

translations.literal: In Duke Huan of Qi's time, though the House of Zhou had declined, it was not like the beginning of the Jian'an era.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Huan's day, though the House of Zhou had waned, the realm had not yet fallen as far as it had at the start of the Jian'an era.

sentences.zh: 建安之初，四海蕩覆，尺土一民，皆非漢有。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an, the four seas were overturned and swept away; every foot of land and every subject no longer belonged to Han.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jian'an, the realm was utterly overturned — not a foot of land nor a single subject truly remained the Han dynasty's.

sentences.zh: 荀彧佐魏武而興之，舉賢用能，訓卒厲兵，決機發策，征伐四克，遂能以弱為強，化亂為治，十分天下而有其八，其功豈在管仲之後乎！

translations.literal: Xun Yu assisted Wei Wu and helped him rise; he raised the worthy and employed the capable, trained soldiers and sharpened weapons, decided strategy and issued plans, and in campaigns conquered on all sides — thus he was able to make the weak strong and transform disorder into order, holding eight tenths of the empire under heaven. Were his achievements behind Guan Zhong's!
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu assisted Cao Cao and helped him rise to power. He raised worthy men and employed the capable, trained armies and sharpened weapons, devised strategy and directed campaigns, and conquered on every front — transforming weakness into strength and chaos into order until eight tenths of the empire lay in Cao Cao's hands. His achievements were surely no less than Guan Zhong's!

sentences.zh: 管仲不死子糾而荀彧死漢室，其仁復居管仲之先矣！

translations.literal: Guan Zhong did not die for Prince Jiu, yet Xun Yu died for the House of Han — his benevolence again stands before Guan Zhong's!
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong did not die for Prince Jiu, yet Xun Yu gave his life for the House of Han — in benevolence he even surpassed Guan Zhong!

sentences.zh: 而杜牧乃以為「彧之勸魏武取兗州則比之高、光，官渡不令還許則比之楚、漢，及事就功畢，乃欲邀名於漢代，譬之教盜穴牆發匱而不與同挈，得不為盜乎？

translations.literal: Yet Du Mu held that "when Yu urged Wei Wu to take Yan Province he was compared to Gao and Guang; at Guandu, when he did not allow return to Xu, he was compared to Chu and Han — and when the enterprise was complete and merit fulfilled, he then wished to win a name under the Han dynasty — like teaching a thief to bore through a wall and break open a chest but not share in carrying the loot; could one say he was not a thief?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Du Mu argued that when Xun Yu urged Cao Cao to seize Yan Province, historians compared him to Emperor Gao and Emperor Guangwu; at Guandu, when he prevented Cao Cao from returning to Xu, they compared the struggle to that of Chu and Han — yet once the enterprise was complete, Xun Yu sought to reclaim a reputation as a loyal servant of Han. This, Du Mu said, was like teaching a thief to break through a wall and raid a chest but refusing to share in carrying off the loot — could such a man be called anything but a thief?

sentences.zh: 」臣以為孔子稱「文勝質則史」，凡為史者記人之言，必有以文之。

translations.literal: " Your subject holds that Confucius said "when ornament surpasses substance, one becomes a mere recorder" — all who write history, when recording men's words, must ornament them with literary art.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Guang replies: Confucius said, "When literary polish exceeds substance, one becomes a mere chronicler." Historians who record men's words invariably dress them in literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 然則比魏武於高、光、楚、漢者，史氏之文也，豈皆彧口所言邪！

translations.literal: In that case, comparing Wei Wu to Gao, Guang, Chu, and Han is the historians' literary art — how could it all be words spoken from Yu's mouth!
translations.idiomatic: The comparisons of Cao Cao to Emperor Gao, Emperor Guangwu, and the contest of Chu and Han are the historian's literary embellishments — they cannot all have been Xun Yu's own words!

sentences.zh: 用是貶彧，非其罪矣。

translations.literal: To use this to denigrate Yu is not his crime.
translations.idiomatic: To denigrate Xun Yu on this basis is to blame him for a crime he did not commit.

sentences.zh: 且使魏武為帝，則彧為佐命元功，與蕭何同賞矣；

translations.literal: Moreover, if Wei Wu became emperor, then Yu would be the founding minister of the mandate, receiving reward equal to Xiao He's;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, had Cao Cao become emperor, Xun Yu would have been honored as a founding minister of the new dynasty, rewarded equally with Xiao He;

sentences.zh: 彧不利此而利於殺身以邀名，豈人情乎！

translations.literal: Yu would not benefit from this yet would benefit from killing himself to win a name — is that human sentiment!
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu would have gained far more from that path than from dying to win a posthumous reputation — such conduct would not accord with human nature!

sentences.zh: 十二月，有星孛於五諸侯。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: a comet appeared at the Five Feudal Lords.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, a comet appeared in the asterism of the Five Feudal Lords.

sentences.zh: 劉備在葭萌，龐統言於備曰：「今陰選精兵，晝夜兼道，逕襲成都，劉璋既不武，又素無豫備，大軍卒至，一舉便定，此上計也。

translations.literal: Liu Bei was at Jiameng; Pang Tong spoke to Bei, saying: "Now secretly select elite troops and march day and night by forced marches, directly raiding Chengdu. Liu Zhang is neither martial nor long prepared against you; when the great army suddenly arrives, it will be settled in one stroke — this is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was at Jiameng when Pang Tong said to him, "Secretly select elite troops and march day and night by forced marches to strike Chengdu directly. Liu Zhang is neither a warrior nor on guard against you. When your army arrives suddenly, the city will fall at a stroke — that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 楊懷、高沛，璋之名將，各杖強兵，據守關頭，聞數有箋諫璋，使發遣將軍還荊州。

translations.literal: Yang Huai and Gao Pei are Zhang's famed generals; each wields strong troops and holds the passes. They have repeatedly sent memorials remonstrating with Zhang, urging him to send the general back to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huai and Gao Pei are Liu Zhang's finest generals. Each commands a strong force and holds the mountain passes. They have repeatedly urged Liu Zhang in writing to send you back to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 將軍遣與相聞，說荊州有急，欲還救之，並使裝束，外作歸形，此二子既服將軍英名，又喜將軍之去，計必乘輕騎來見將軍，因此執之，進取其兵，乃向成都，此中計也。

translations.literal: The general should send word to them, saying Jingzhou is in urgent peril and you wish to return to rescue it, and at the same time have your troops prepare equipment and outwardly show the appearance of withdrawal. These two men, having submitted to the general's heroic name and also delighting in the general's departure, will surely come with light cavalry to see the general — seize them thereby, take their troops, and then advance on Chengdu. This is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: Send word to them that Jingzhou is in urgent peril and you must return to its rescue, and have your troops pack for departure so that your withdrawal looks genuine. These two men admire your reputation and will be glad to see you go — they will surely ride out with a small escort to see you off. Seize them, take their troops, and march on Chengdu. That is the second plan.

sentences.zh: 退還白帝，連引荊州，徐還圖之，此下計也。

translations.literal: Withdraw to Baidi, link up with Jingzhou, and slowly return to plot further — this is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw to Baidi, link up with Jingzhou, and bide your time — that is the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 若沉吟下去，將致大困，不可久矣。

translations.literal: If you hesitate and delay, you will fall into great difficulty and cannot long remain.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and delay, you will soon be trapped in dire straits and cannot hold out much longer.

sentences.zh: 」備然其中計。

translations.literal: " Bei approved the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei approved the middle plan.

sentences.zh: 及曹操攻孫權，權呼備自救。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao attacked Sun Quan, Quan called on Bei to rescue himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao attacked Sun Quan, Sun Quan called on Liu Bei to come to his aid.

sentences.zh: 備貽璋書曰：「孫氏與孤本為脣齒，而關羽兵弱，今不往救，則曹操必取荊州，轉侵州界，其憂甚於張魯。

translations.literal: Bei sent Zhang a letter, saying: "The Sun clan and I are originally lip and teeth, yet Guan Yu's troops are weak. If I do not go now to rescue them, Cao Cao will surely take Jingzhou and turn to invade your borders — that worry is greater than Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei wrote to Liu Zhang, saying, "The Sun clan and I are bound together like lip and teeth, yet Guan Yu's forces are weak. If I do not go to their rescue now, Cao Cao will surely seize Jingzhou and then turn to invade your borders — a far greater threat than Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 魯自守之賊，不足慮也。

translations.literal: Lu is a bandit who holds his own territory; he is not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu is merely a local rebel holding his own territory — he is not worth worrying over.

sentences.zh: 」因求益萬兵及資糧，璋但許兵四千，其餘皆給半。

translations.literal: " He then requested ten thousand additional troops and supplies; Zhang granted only four thousand troops, and gave only half of the rest.
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked for ten thousand more troops and additional supplies. Liu Zhang granted only four thousand troops and half of everything else requested.

sentences.zh: 備因激怒其眾曰：「吾為益州征強敵，師徒勤瘁，而積財吝賞，何以使士大夫死戰乎！

translations.literal: Bei thereupon incited his troops to anger, saying: "I campaign for Yizhou against strong enemies; the army toils in hardship, yet he hoards wealth and is stingy with rewards — how can this make officers and gentlemen die fighting!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei then roused his troops to anger, saying, "I fight powerful enemies on Yizhou's behalf while my army suffers hardship, yet Liu Zhang hoards his wealth and is miserly with rewards — how can he expect his officers and men to die for him!"

sentences.zh: 」張松書與備及法正曰：「今大事垂立，如何釋此去乎！

translations.literal: " Zhang Song wrote to Bei and Fa Zheng, saying: "The great enterprise is on the verge of success — how can you abandon it and leave!"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Song wrote to Liu Bei and Fa Zheng, saying, "Our great enterprise is on the verge of success — how can you abandon it and leave!"

sentences.zh: 」松兄廣漢太宗肅，恐禍及己，因發其謀。

translations.literal: Song's elder brother Zong of Guanghan, Su Su, fearing calamity would reach himself, thereupon exposed the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Song's elder brother Zhang Su of Guanghan, fearing the plot would implicate him, exposed it.

sentences.zh: 於是璋收斬松，敕關戍諸將文書皆勿復得與備關通。

translations.literal: Zhang thereupon arrested and executed Song, and ordered the garrison commanders at the passes that none of their documents might again reach Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang then arrested and executed Zhang Song, and ordered the garrison commanders at the passes to cut off all communication with Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備大怒，召璋白水軍督楊懷、高沛，責以無禮，斬之；

translations.literal: Bei was greatly angered; he summoned Zhang's Baishui Army Supervisor Yang Huai and Gao Pei, rebuked them for discourtesy, and executed them;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was furious. He summoned Liu Zhang's supervisors of the Baishui garrison, Yang Huai and Gao Pei, rebuked them for their discourtesy, and executed them;

sentences.zh: 勒兵徑至關頭，並其兵，進據涪城。

translations.literal: he led his troops straight to the passes, absorbed their forces, and advanced to occupy Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: then led his army straight to the passes, absorbed their troops, and advanced to occupy Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇帝辛建安十八年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xian of Han [xin], Jian'an eighteenth year (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian of Han [xin], eighteenth year of Jian'an (

sentences.zh: 癸巳，公元二一三年）

translations.literal: Guisi, AD 213)
translations.idiomatic: Guisi, AD 213)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曹操進軍濡須口，號步騎四十萬，攻破孫權江西營，獲其都督公孫陽。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Cao Cao advanced his army to the Ruxu river mouth, claiming forty thousand infantry and cavalry; he broke through Sun Quan's camp west of the river and captured his commander Gongsun Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Cao Cao advanced to the Ruxu river mouth at the head of what he claimed were forty thousand infantry and cavalry. He broke through Sun Quan's camp west of the river and captured his commander Gongsun Yang.

sentences.zh: 權率眾七萬御之，相守月餘。

translations.literal: Quan led seventy thousand men to resist him; they faced each other for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan led seventy thousand men to resist him, and the two armies faced each other for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 操見其舟船器仗軍伍整肅，歎曰：「生子當如孫仲謀；

translations.literal: Cao saw his boats, weapons, and military formations were orderly and strict, and sighed, saying: "When one begets a son, let him be like Sun Zhongmou;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao saw that Sun Quan's boats, weapons, and formations were disciplined and orderly, and sighed, "When one begets a son, let him be like Sun Zhongmou;

sentences.zh: 如劉景升兒子，豚犬耳！

translations.literal: like Liu Jingsheng's sons — pigs and dogs!"
translations.idiomatic: not like Liu Jingsheng's sons — mere pigs and dogs!"

sentences.zh: 」權為箋與操，說：「春水方生，公宜速去。

translations.literal: " Quan sent a letter to Cao, saying: "The spring waters are rising — my lord should quickly depart.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan sent Cao Cao a letter saying, "The spring floods are rising — you should withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 」別紙言：「足下不死，孤不得安。

translations.literal: " On a separate sheet he wrote: "So long as you do not die, I cannot be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " On a separate sheet he added, "So long as you do not die, I cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 」操語諸將曰：「孫權不欺孤。

translations.literal: " Cao said to his generals: "Sun Quan does not deceive me.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao told his generals, "Sun Quan does not lie to me.

sentences.zh: 」乃徹軍還。

translations.literal: " He then withdrew his army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He then withdrew his army and returned.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔並十四州，復為九州。

translations.literal: Gengyin: an edict merged the fourteen provinces back into nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengyin, an edict restored the former division of the empire into nine provinces, abolishing the fourteen-province system.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，曹操至鄴。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Cao Cao reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Cao Cao reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，曹操在譙，恐濱江郡縣為孫權所略，欲徙令近內，以問揚州別駕蔣濟，曰：「昔孤與袁本初對軍官渡，徙燕、白馬民，民不得走，賊亦不敢鈔。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cao Cao was at Qiao, fearing that commanderies and counties along the river would be plundered by Sun Quan, he wished to relocate the people inland and asked Yangzhou Vice-Director Jiang Ji, saying: "In the past when I faced Yuan Benchu across the army at Guandu, I relocated the people of Yan and Baima; the people could not flee, and the bandits also did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cao Cao was at Qiao, he feared that the riverine commanderies and counties would be plundered by Sun Quan and wished to relocate the people inland. He asked Yangzhou Vice-Director Jiang Ji, "When I faced Yuan Shao across the field at Guandu, I relocated the people of Yan and Baima. They could not flee, and the enemy did not dare raid them.

sentences.zh: 今欲徙淮南民，何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to relocate the people of Huainan — what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to relocate the people of Huainan — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「是時兵弱賊強，不徙必失之。

translations.literal: He replied: "At that time our troops were weak and the bandits strong; if we did not relocate them we would surely lose them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji replied, "At that time our forces were weak and the enemy strong — if we had not relocated those people, we would surely have lost them.

sentences.zh: 自破袁紹以來，明公威震天下，民無他志，人情懷土，實不樂徙，懼必不安。

translations.literal: Since defeating Yuan Shao, my lord's prestige has shaken the empire; the people have no other intent. Human sentiment clings to native soil — they truly do not delight in relocation, and I fear they will surely be unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Since you defeated Yuan Shao, your prestige has shaken the empire and the people have no wish to leave their homes. Men cling to the land where they were born — they will not willingly move, and I fear the relocation will only unsettle them.

sentences.zh: 」操不從。

translations.literal: " Cao did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 既而民轉相驚，自廬江、九江、蘄春、廣陵，戶十餘萬皆東流江，江西遂虛，合淝以南，惟有皖城。

translations.literal: Before long the people began alarming one another in turn; from Lujiang, Jiujiang, Qichun, and Guangling, more than a hundred thousand households all flowed east across the river. The region west of the river was then emptied; south of Hefei, only Wancheng remained.
translations.idiomatic: Before long panic spread among the people. From Lujiang, Jiujiang, Qichun, and Guangling, more than a hundred thousand households fled east across the Yangzi. The region west of the river was emptied, and south of Hefei only Wancheng remained.

sentences.zh: 濟後奉使詣鄴，操迎見，大笑曰：「本但欲使避賊，乃更驅盡之！

translations.literal: Later, when Ji went on mission to Ye, Cao received him and laughed greatly, saying: "I originally only wished to have them avoid the bandits — yet instead I drove them all away!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Ji later went on mission to Ye, Cao Cao received him with a great laugh and said, "I only meant to help them escape the enemy — and instead I drove them all away!"

sentences.zh: 」拜濟丹楊太守。

translations.literal: He appointed Ji Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Jiang Ji Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，以冀州十郡封曹操為魏公，以丞相領冀州牧如故。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Bingshen: ten commanderies of Jizhou were enfeoffed to Cao Cao as Duke of Wei, while he continued as Chancellor holding the governorship of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day Bingshen, ten commanderies of Jizhou were enfeoffed to Cao Cao as Duke of Wei, while he continued to serve as Chancellor and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 又加九錫：大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟；

translations.literal: He was also granted the nine bestowals: one great chariot and one war chariot; two teams of four black stallions;
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted the nine insignia of honor: a great chariot and a war chariot; two teams of four black stallions;

sentences.zh: 兗冕之服，赤舄副焉；

translations.literal: robes and cap of the nine emblems, with red slippers to match;
translations.idiomatic: robes and cap embroidered with the nine emblems, with matching red slippers;

sentences.zh: 軒縣之樂，八佾之舞；

translations.literal: the music of suspended bells, and the dance of eight rows;
translations.idiomatic: the music of suspended bells and the dance of eight rows;

sentences.zh: 朱戶以居；

translations.literal: vermilion gateposts for his residence;
translations.idiomatic: vermilion gateposts for his residence;

sentences.zh: 納陛以登；

translations.literal: a ramp for ascending;
translations.idiomatic: a ramp for ascending;

sentences.zh: 虎賁之士三百人；

translations.literal: three hundred tiger-guard warriors;
translations.idiomatic: three hundred tiger-guard warriors;

sentences.zh: 鈇、鉞各一；

translations.literal: one axe and one battle-axe;
translations.idiomatic: one axe and one ceremonial battle-axe;

sentences.zh: 彤弓一，彤矢百，玈弓十，玈矢千；

translations.literal: one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows;
translations.idiomatic: one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, and one thousand black arrows;

sentences.zh: 秬鬯一卣，珪、瓚副焉。

translations.literal: one jar of black millet ale, with jade scepter and libation cup to match.
translations.idiomatic: one jar of black millet ale, with a jade scepter and libation cup to match.

sentences.zh: 大雨水。

translations.literal: Great rains fell.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains fell.

sentences.zh: 益州從事廣漢鄭度聞劉備舉兵，謂劉璋曰：「左將軍懸軍襲我，兵不滿萬，士眾未附，軍無輜重，野谷是資。

translations.literal: Attendant Zheng Du of Guanghan in Yizhou, hearing that Liu Bei had raised troops, said to Liu Zhang: "General of the Left Bei leads an isolated army in a surprise attack upon us; his troops number less than ten thousand, his soldiers are not yet attached to him, and the army has no baggage train — wild grain is his supply.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Du, an Attendant of Guanghan in Yizhou, hearing that Liu Bei had taken up arms, said to Liu Zhang, "General Liu of the Left leads an isolated force in a surprise attack. His army numbers fewer than ten thousand, his men are not yet loyal to him, and he has no baggage train — he must live off the wild grain of the countryside.

sentences.zh: 其計莫若盡驅巴西、梓潼民內、涪水以西，其倉廩野谷，一皆燒除，高壘深溝，靜以待之。

translations.literal: The best plan is to drive all the people of Baxi and Zitong inland west of the Fu River, burn all granaries and wild grain, build high ramparts and deep ditches, and wait quietly.
translations.idiomatic: The best plan is to drive all the people of Baxi and Zitong inland west of the Fu River, burn every granary and field of wild grain, build high ramparts and deep ditches, and wait quietly.

sentences.zh: 彼至，請戰勿許。

translations.literal: When they arrive, do not grant battle if they request it.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrive, refuse battle even if they challenge you.

sentences.zh: 久無所資，不過百日，必將自走，走而擊之，此必禽耳。

translations.literal: Long without supplies, within no more than a hundred days they will surely flee of themselves; strike them as they flee, and they will surely be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of supplies for no more than a hundred days, they will surely flee on their own. Strike them as they retreat, and you will surely capture them.

sentences.zh: 」劉備聞而惡之，以問法正。

translations.literal: " When Bei heard of this he hated it, and asked Fa Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: " When Liu Bei heard of this plan he was alarmed and asked Fa Zheng about it.

sentences.zh: 正曰：「璋終不能用，無憂也。

translations.literal: Zheng said: "Zhang will ultimately not use it — no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng said, "Liu Zhang will never adopt it — have no fear.

sentences.zh: 」璋果謂其群下曰：「吾聞拒敵以安民，未聞動民以避敵也。

translations.literal: " Zhang indeed said to his subordinates: "I have heard that one repels the enemy to secure the people — I have never heard of disturbing the people to avoid the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Zhang indeed told his subordinates, "I have heard that one repels the enemy to protect the people — I have never heard of harming the people to avoid an enemy.

sentences.zh: 」不用度計。

translations.literal: " He did not adopt Du's plan.
translations.idiomatic: " He rejected Zheng Du's plan.

sentences.zh: 璋遣其將劉瑰、冷苞、張任、鄧賢、吳懿等拒備，皆敗，退保綿竹；

translations.literal: Zhang sent his generals Liu Gui, Leng Bao, Zhang Ren, Deng Xian, Wu Yi, and others to resist Bei; all were defeated and withdrew to hold Mianzhu;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang sent his generals Liu Gui, Leng Bao, Zhang Ren, Deng Xian, Wu Yi, and others to resist Liu Bei. All were defeated and withdrew to hold Mianzhu;

sentences.zh: 懿詣軍降。

translations.literal: Yi came to the army and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yi came to Liu Bei's camp and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 璋復遣護軍南陽李嚴、江夏費觀督綿竹諸軍，嚴、觀亦率其眾降於備。

translations.literal: Zhang again sent Protector of the Army Li Yan of Nanyang and Fei Guan of Jiangxia to command the armies at Mianzhu; Yan and Guan also led their troops to surrender to Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang again sent Protector of the Army Li Yan of Nanyang and Fei Guan of Jiangxia to command the armies at Mianzhu. Li Yan and Fei Guan also led their troops to surrender to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備軍益強，分遣諸將平下屬縣。

translations.literal: Bei's army grew ever stronger; he dispatched generals in separate columns to pacify the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's army grew ever stronger, and he dispatched his generals in separate columns to pacify the subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 劉瑰、張任與璋子循退守雒城，備進軍圍之。

translations.literal: Liu Gui, Zhang Ren, and Zhang's son Xun withdrew to hold Luocheng; Bei advanced his army to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, Zhang Ren, and Liu Zhang's son Liu Xun withdrew to hold Luocheng. Liu Bei advanced and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 任勒兵出戰於雁橋，軍敗，任死。

translations.literal: Ren led troops out to battle at Wild Goose Bridge; the army was defeated and Ren died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ren led his troops out to fight at Wild Goose Bridge. His army was defeated and Zhang Ren was killed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏始建社稷、宗廟。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Wei first established altars to the soil and grain and ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wei first established altars to the soil and grain and ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 魏公操納三女為貴人。

translations.literal: Duke Cao of Wei took three daughters as Noble Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cao of Wei took three daughters into the palace as Noble Ladies.

sentences.zh: 初，魏公操追馬超至安定，聞田銀、蘇伯反，引軍還。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Duke Cao of Wei pursued Ma Chao to Anding, he heard that Tian Yin and Su Bo had rebelled and led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Duke Cao of Wei pursued Ma Chao to Anding, he heard that Tian Yin and Su Bo had rebelled and turned his army back.

sentences.zh: 參涼州軍事楊阜言於操曰：「超有信、布之勇，甚得羌、胡心；

translations.literal: Yang Fu, who participated in Liangzhou military affairs, spoke to Cao, saying: "Chao has the courage of Xin and Bu and has deeply won the hearts of the Qiang and Hu;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, who participated in Liangzhou military affairs, said to Cao Cao, "Ma Chao has the courage of Xin and Bu and has deeply won the hearts of the Qiang and Hu;

sentences.zh: 若大軍還，不設備，隴上諸郡非國家之有也。

translations.literal: if the great army returns without making preparations, the commanderies of Longshang will no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: if your main army withdraws without making preparations, the commanderies of Longshang will no longer belong to the state.

sentences.zh: 」操還，超果率羌、胡擊隴上諸郡縣，郡縣皆應之，惟冀城奉州郡以固守。

translations.literal: " When Cao returned, Chao indeed led the Qiang and Hu to attack the commanderies and counties of Longshang; the commanderies and counties all responded to him — only Jicheng, upholding the province and commandery, held firm.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao withdrew, and Ma Chao indeed led the Qiang and Hu to attack the commanderies and counties of Longshang. The commanderies and counties all rose in response — only Jicheng, loyal to the provincial and commandery authorities, held firm.

sentences.zh: 超盡兼隴右之眾，張魯復遣大將楊昂助之，凡萬餘人，攻冀城，自正月至八月，救兵不至。

translations.literal: Chao mustered all the forces of Longyou; Zhang Lu again sent his great general Yang Ang to assist him—more than ten thousand in all—attacking Jicheng. From the first month through the eighth month relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao mustered all the forces of Longyou. Zhang Lu again sent his great general Yang Ang to assist him—more than ten thousand men in all—attacking Jicheng. From the first month through the eighth month, no relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 刺史韋康遣別駕閻溫出，告急於夏侯淵，外圍數重，溫夜從水中潛出。

translations.literal: Inspector Wei Kang sent Vice-Director Yan Wen out to report the emergency to Xiahou Yuan; the outer encirclement was many layers deep, and Wen slipped out by water at night.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wei Kang sent Vice-Director Yan Wen out to report the emergency to Xiahou Yuan. The outer encirclement was many layers deep, and Wen slipped out through the water at night.

sentences.zh: 明日，超兵見其跡，遣追獲之。

translations.literal: The next day Chao's troops saw his tracks and sent pursuers who captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ma Chao's troops saw his tracks and sent pursuers who captured him.

sentences.zh: 超載溫詣城下，使告城中云：「東方無救。

translations.literal: Chao loaded Wen and brought him below the city, making him tell those inside: "There is no relief from the east.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao loaded Wen onto a cart and brought him below the city, making him tell those inside: "There is no relief from the east.

sentences.zh: 」溫向城大呼曰：「大軍不過三日至，勉之！

translations.literal: " Wen shouted toward the city: "The great army will arrive within three days at most—take heart!
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Wen shouted toward the city: "The great army will arrive within three days at most—take heart!

sentences.zh: 」城中皆泣，稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " Those in the city all wept and cried "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: " Those in the city all wept and cried "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 超雖怒，猶以攻城久不下，徐徐更誘溫，冀其改意。

translations.literal: Though Chao was angry, because the siege had long failed to take the city he gradually tried to entice Wen further, hoping he would change his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ma Chao was angry, because the siege had long failed to take the city he gradually tried to entice Wen further, hoping he would change his mind.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「事君有死無二，而卿乃欲令長者出不義之言乎！

translations.literal: Wen said: "Serving one's lord—there is death but no second loyalty. Yet you would have an elder speak unrighteous words!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wen said: "Serving one's lord—there is death but no second loyalty. Yet you would have an elder speak unrighteous words!

sentences.zh: 」超遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Chao then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Chao then killed him.

sentences.zh: 已而外救不至，韋康太守欲降。

translations.literal: Before long outside relief did not arrive; Grand Administrator Wei Kang wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long outside relief did not arrive. Grand Administrator Wei Kang wished to surrender.

sentences.zh: 楊阜號哭諫曰：「阜等率父兄子弟以義相勵，有死無二，以為使君守此城。

translations.literal: Yang Fu wailed and remonstrated: "Fu and others led fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers, roused by righteousness—death but no second loyalty—to hold this city for our lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu wailed and remonstrated: "Fu and others led fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers, roused by righteousness—death but no second loyalty—to hold this city for our lord.

sentences.zh: 今奈何棄垂成之功，陷不義之名乎！

translations.literal: Now how can we abandon a nearly completed achievement and fall into an unrighteous name!
translations.idiomatic: Now how can we abandon a nearly completed achievement and fall into an unrighteous name!

sentences.zh: 」刺史、太守不聽，開城門迎超。

translations.literal: " The Inspector and Grand Administrator would not listen and opened the city gates to welcome Chao.
translations.idiomatic: " The inspector and grand administrator would not listen and opened the city gates to welcome Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超入，遂殺刺史、太守，自稱征西將軍、領并州牧、督涼州軍事。

translations.literal: Chao entered and then killed the Inspector and Grand Administrator, styling himself General Who Subdues the West, holding the governorship of Bing province and supervising Liang province military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao entered and then killed the inspector and grand administrator, styling himself General Who Subdues the West, holding the governorship of Bing province and supervising Liang province military affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏公操便夏侯淵救冀，未到而冀敗。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Cao sent Xiahou Yuan to rescue Jicheng; he had not arrived when Jicheng fell.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Wei Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan to rescue Jicheng. He had not arrived when Jicheng fell.

sentences.zh: 淵去冀二百餘里，超來逆戰，淵軍不利。

translations.literal: Yuan was more than two hundred li from Jicheng when Chao came to meet him in battle and Yuan's army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was more than two hundred li from Jicheng when Ma Chao came to meet him in battle and Yuan's army fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 氐王千萬反應超，屯興國，淵引軍還。

translations.literal: The Di king Qianwan responded to Chao and encamped at Xingguo; Yuan led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: The Di king Qianwan responded to Ma Chao and encamped at Xingguo. Yuan led his army back.

sentences.zh: 會楊阜喪妻，就超求假以葬之。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Fu's wife died; he asked Chao for leave to bury her.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Yang Fu's wife died. He asked Ma Chao for leave to bury her.

sentences.zh: 阜外兄天水姜敘為撫夷將軍，擁兵屯歷城。

translations.literal: Fu's wife's elder brother from Tianshui, Jiang Xu, served as General Who Pacifies the Yi, holding troops encamped at Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's wife's elder brother from Tianshui, Jiang Xu, served as General Who Pacifies the Yi, holding troops encamped at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 阜見敘及其母，歔欷悲甚。

translations.literal: When Fu saw Xu and his mother he sobbed and grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu saw Xu and his mother he sobbed and grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 敘曰：「何為乃爾？

translations.literal: Xu said: "Why are you like this?
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "Why are you like this?

sentences.zh: 」阜曰：「守城不能完，君亡不能死，亦何面目以視息於天下！

translations.literal: " Fu said: "I could not complete the defense of the city, and when our lord died I could not die with him—what face have I to draw breath under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: " Fu said: "I could not complete the defense of the city, and when our lord died I could not die with him—what face have I to draw breath under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 馬超背父叛君，虐殺州將，豈獨阜之憂責，一州士大夫皆蒙其恥。

translations.literal: Ma Chao turned against his father and rebelled against his lord, cruelly killing the provincial commander—not Fu's worry and blame alone; the scholars and officials of the whole province all bear this shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao turned against his father and rebelled against his lord, cruelly killing the provincial commander—not Fu's worry and blame alone. The scholars and officials of the whole province all bear this shame.

sentences.zh: 君擁兵專制而無討賊心，此趙盾所以書弒君也。

translations.literal: You hold troops and act on your own authority yet have no heart to punish the traitor—this is why Zhao Dun was recorded as having assassinated his lord.
translations.idiomatic: You hold troops and act on your own authority yet have no heart to punish the traitor—this is why Zhao Dun was recorded as having assassinated his lord.

sentences.zh: 超強而無義，多釁，易圖耳。

translations.literal: Chao is strong but without righteousness, full of offenses—he is easy to plot against.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao is strong but without righteousness, full of offenses—he is easy to plot against.

sentences.zh: 」敘母慨然曰：「咄！

translations.literal: " Xu's mother said with indignation: "Tsk!
translations.idiomatic: " Xu's mother said with indignation: "Tsk!

sentences.zh: 伯奕，韋伯君遇難，亦汝之負，豈獨義山哉！

translations.literal: Boyi, when Lord Wei met calamity, that was your burden too—not Yishan's alone!
translations.idiomatic: Boyi, when Lord Wei met calamity, that was your burden too—not Yishan's alone!

sentences.zh: 人誰不死，死於忠義，得其所也。

translations.literal: Who does not die? To die for loyalty and righteousness is to die in the right place.
translations.idiomatic: Who does not die? To die for loyalty and righteousness is to die in the right place.

sentences.zh: 但當速發，勿復顧我；

translations.literal: Only hurry to act—do not again worry over me;
translations.idiomatic: Only hurry to act—do not again worry over me;

sentences.zh: 我自為汝當之，不以餘年累汝也。

translations.literal: I myself will answer for you and will not burden you with my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: I myself will answer for you and will not burden you with my remaining years.

sentences.zh: 」敘乃與同郡趙昂、尹奉、武都李俊等合謀討超，又使人至冀，結安定梁寬、南安趙衢使為內應。

translations.literal: " Xu then joined with Zhao Ang, Yin Feng, Li Jun of Wudu, and others of his commandery in a plot to attack Chao, and also sent men to Jicheng to win Liang Kuan of Anding and Zhao Qu of Nan'an as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu then joined with Zhao Ang, Yin Feng, Li Jun of Wudu, and others of his commandery in a plot to attack Ma Chao, and also sent men to Jicheng to win Liang Kuan of Anding and Zhao Qu of Nan'an as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 超取趙昂子月為質，昂謂妻異曰：「吾謀如是，事必萬全，當奈月何？

translations.literal: Chao took Zhao Ang's son Yue as hostage; Ang said to his wife Yi: "My plan is thus—the affair is sure to succeed in every way. What shall we do about Yue?
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao took Zhao Ang's son Yue as hostage. Ang said to his wife Yi: "My plan is thus—the affair is sure to succeed in every way. What shall we do about Yue?

sentences.zh: 」異厲聲應曰：「雪君父之大恥，喪元不足為重，況一子哉！

translations.literal: " Yi answered in a stern voice: "To wipe away the great shame of lord and father—losing one's life is not weighty; how much less one son!
translations.idiomatic: " Yi answered in a stern voice: "To wipe away the great shame of lord and father—losing one's life is not weighty. How much less one son!

sentences.zh: 九月，阜與敘進兵，入鹵城，昂、奉據祁山，以討超。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Fu and Xu advanced their troops into Lucheng; Ang and Feng held Qishan to attack Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Fu and Xu advanced their troops into Lucheng. Ang and Feng held Qishan to attack Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 超聞之，大怒，趙衢因譎說超，使自出擊之。

translations.literal: When Chao heard of it he was greatly enraged; Zhao Qu by deceit urged Chao to go out and attack them himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao heard of it he was greatly enraged. Zhao Qu by deceit urged Ma Chao to go out and attack them himself.

sentences.zh: 超出，衢與梁寬閉冀城門，盡殺超妻子。

translations.literal: When Chao went out, Qu and Liang Kuan closed the gates of Jicheng and killed all of Chao's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Chao went out, Qu and Liang Kuan closed the gates of Jicheng and killed all of Ma Chao's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 超進退失據，乃襲歷城，得敘母。

translations.literal: Chao lost his footing in advance and retreat and then raided Licheng, capturing Xu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao lost his footing in advance and retreat and then raided Licheng, capturing Xu's mother.

sentences.zh: 敘母罵之曰：「汝背父之逆子，殺君之桀賊，天地豈久容汝！

translations.literal: Xu's mother cursed him: "You are a traitor son who turned against your father, a violent traitor who killed your lord—Heaven and Earth cannot long tolerate you!
translations.idiomatic: Xu's mother cursed him: "You are a traitor son who turned against your father, a violent traitor who killed your lord—Heaven and Earth cannot long tolerate you!

sentences.zh: 而不早死，敢以面目視人乎！

translations.literal: Yet you do not die early—you dare show your face to others!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you do not die early—you dare show your face to others!

sentences.zh: 」超殺之，又殺趙昂之子月。

translations.literal: " Chao killed her and also killed Zhao Ang's son Yue.
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Chao killed her and also killed Zhao Ang's son Yue.

sentences.zh: 楊阜與超戰，身被五創。

translations.literal: Yang Fu fought Chao and received five wounds on his body.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu fought Ma Chao and received five wounds on his body.

sentences.zh: 超兵敗，遂南奔張魯。

translations.literal: Chao's army was defeated and he fled south to Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao's army was defeated and he fled south to Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 魯以超為都講祭酒，欲妻之以女。

translations.literal: Lu made Chao Director of Lectures and Sacrificial Offerings and wished to give him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu made Ma Chao Director of Lectures and Sacrificial Offerings and wished to give him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 或謂魯曰：「有人若此，不愛其親，焉能愛人！

translations.literal: Someone said to Lu: "A man like this—if he does not love his own kin, how can he love others!
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Zhang Lu: "A man like this—if he does not love his own kin, how can he love others!

sentences.zh: 」魯乃止。

translations.literal: " Lu then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Lu then desisted.

sentences.zh: 操封討超之功，侯者十一人，賜楊阜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Cao enfeoffed those who had merit in attacking Chao—eleven men as marquises—and granted Yang Fu the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao enfeoffed those who had merit in attacking Ma Chao—eleven men as marquises—and granted Yang Fu the rank of Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，魏初置尚書、侍中、六卿；

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, Wei for the first time established Masters of Writing, Palace Attendants, and the Six Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the eleventh month, Wei for the first time established Masters of Writing, Palace Attendants, and the Six Ministers;

sentences.zh: 以荀攸為尚書令，涼茂為僕射，毛玠、崔琰、常林、徐奕、何夔為尚書，王粲、杜襲、衛覬、和洽為侍中，鐘繇為大理，王修為大司農，袁渙為郎中令、行御史大夫事，陳群為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Xun You was made Director of the Masters of Writing, Liang Mao Vice Director, Mao Jie, Cui Yan, Chang Lin, Xu Yi, and He Kui Masters of Writing, Wang Can, Du Xi, Wei Ji, and He Qia Palace Attendants, Zhong Yao Director of the Court of Justice, Wang Xiu Director of the Grand Granary, Yuan Huan Director of the Palace Secretariat acting as Grand Master of Works, and Chen Qun Vice Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Xun You was made Director of the Masters of Writing, Liang Mao Vice Director, Mao Jie, Cui Yan, Chang Lin, Xu Yi, and He Kui Masters of Writing, Wang Can, Du Xi, Wei Ji, and He Qia Palace Attendants, Zhong Yao Director of the Court of Justice, Wang Xiu Director of the Grand Granary, Yuan Huan Director of the Palace Secretariat acting as Grand Master of Works, and Chen Qun Vice Director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 袁渙得賞賜，皆散之，家無所儲，乏則取之於人，不為皦察之行，然時人皆服其清。

translations.literal: Yuan Huan received rewards and bestowals and distributed them all; his household had no stores, and when in want he took from others—he did not practice conduct of minute scrutiny, yet the men of the time all submitted to his purity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huan received rewards and bestowals and distributed them all. His household had no stores, and when in want he took from others. He did not practice conduct of minute scrutiny, yet the men of the time all submitted to his purity.

sentences.zh: 時有傳劉備死者，群臣皆賀，唯渙獨否。

translations.literal: At that time there was a rumor that Liu Bei had died; the ministers all congratulated, but Huan alone did not.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a rumor that Liu Bei had died. The ministers all congratulated, but Huan alone did not.

sentences.zh: 魏公操欲復肉刑，令曰：「昔陳鴻臚以為死刑有可加於仁恩者，御史中丞能申其父之論乎？

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Cao wished to restore corporal punishment and issued an order: "In former times Palace Attendant Chen believed that capital punishment could be added to benevolent grace. Can the Vice Director of the Censorate set forth his father's argument?
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Wei Cao Cao wished to restore corporal punishment and issued an order: "In former times Palace Attendant Chen believed that capital punishment could be added to benevolent grace. Can the Vice Director of the Censorate set forth his father's argument?

sentences.zh: 」陳群對曰：「臣父紀以為漢除肉刑而增加於笞，本興仁惻而死者更眾，所謂名輕而實重者也。

translations.literal: " Chen Qun replied: "My late father Ji held that when Han abolished corporal punishment and increased flogging, it was originally to raise benevolent compassion yet the dead became more numerous—what is called a light name but a heavy reality.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Qun replied: "My late father Ji held that when Han abolished corporal punishment and increased flogging, it was originally to raise benevolent compassion, yet the dead became more numerous—what is called a light name but a heavy reality.

sentences.zh: 名輕則易犯，實重則傷民。

translations.literal: When the name is light, offenses are easy to commit; when the reality is heavy, the people are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the name is light, offenses are easy to commit. When the reality is heavy, the people are harmed.

sentences.zh: 且殺人償死，合於古制；

translations.literal: Moreover, killing repays killing—this accords with ancient regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, killing repays killing—this accords with ancient regulation;

sentences.zh: 至於傷人，或殘毀其體，而裁翦毛髮，非其理也。

translations.literal: as for injuring a person, sometimes mutilating the body yet only trimming hair and beard—this is not reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: as for injuring a person, sometimes mutilating the body yet only trimming hair and beard—this is not reasonable.

sentences.zh: 若用古刑，使淫者下蠶室，盜者刖其足，則永無淫放穿窬之奸矣。

translations.literal: If ancient punishments were used, making the licentious enter the silkworm chamber and cutting off the feet of thieves, then there would forever be no licentiousness, robbery, or burglary.
translations.idiomatic: If ancient punishments were used, making the licentious enter the silkworm chamber and cutting off the feet of thieves, then there would forever be no licentiousness, robbery, or burglary.

sentences.zh: 夫三千之屬，雖末可悉復，若斯數者，時之所患，宜先施用。

translations.literal: Of the three thousand categories, though not all can be fully restored, for such numbers as these—the troubles of the time—it is fitting to apply them first.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three thousand categories, though not all can be fully restored, for such numbers as these—the troubles of the time—it is fitting to apply them first.

sentences.zh: 漢律所殺，殊死之罪，仁所不及也，其餘逮死者，可易以肉刑。

translations.literal: Among Han statutes for killing, the crime of special death is beyond the reach of benevolence; for the rest who face death, corporal punishment may replace it.
translations.idiomatic: Among Han statutes for killing, the crime of special death is beyond the reach of benevolence. For the rest who face death, corporal punishment may replace it.

sentences.zh: 如此，則所刑之與所生足以相貿矣。

translations.literal: Thus the punishment applied and the life preserved would be enough to balance each other.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the punishment applied and the life preserved would be enough to balance each other.

sentences.zh: 今以笞死之法易不殺之刑，是重人支體而輕人軀命也。

translations.literal: Now to replace punishments that do not kill with the flogging-to-death law is to value men's limbs lightly and value men's lives heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Now to replace punishments that do not kill with the flogging-to-death law is to value men's limbs lightly and value men's lives heavily.

sentences.zh: 」當時議者，唯鐘繇與群議同，餘皆以為未可行。

translations.literal: " Among those who deliberated at the time, only Zhong Yao agreed with Qun; the rest all held it could not yet be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Among those who deliberated at the time, only Zhong Yao agreed with Qun. The rest all held it could not yet be carried out.

sentences.zh: 操以軍事未罷，顧眾議而止。

translations.literal: Cao, because military affairs had not ceased, looked to the assembly's opinion and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, because military affairs had not ceased, looked to the assembly's opinion and stopped.
